Scenario5Start.3.full: The siblings' arrival to claim their considerable inheritance was met with the indifference of a murky countryside, gray and overcast. The sky was heavy with moisture, but could not crack into a tempest, as if heralding the unfortunate circumstances to which they would soon find themselves.
Scenario5Start.3.easy: The brothers and sisters came to the village to claim their large inheritance. The countryside was dark and gray, and nobody cared that they had arrived. Heavy clouds hung in the sky, but the storm never came. It was as if the weather knew that bad times were coming.
Scenario5Start.3.short: The siblings arrived to claim their inheritance beneath a heavy, gray sky that promised misfortune.

Scenario5Start.4.full: Upon reaching the village, a foul stench tinged the air as teams of horses pulled the charcoal wagons like a silent funeral procession through the muddy streets. Emaciated peasants shielded their faces from the ashen gloom, seemingly unbothered by the display, and went about their somber activities uninterrupted. Several canvas-bound carts lined the edges of the main road, the dismal, gray skin of a human foot sometimes dangling freely from a rip in the fabric.
Scenario5Start.4.easy: When they reached the village, the air smelled terrible. Horses slowly pulled wagons full of charcoal through the muddy streets, like a silent funeral. Thin, hungry villagers covered their faces against the gray ash. They did not seem to care, and they went on with their sad work. Carts covered with cloth stood along the main road. Sometimes the gray foot of a dead person hung out through a hole in the cloth.
Scenario5Start.4.short: The village stank. Charcoal wagons crawled through the mud like a funeral procession, and from the covered carts along the road a gray, lifeless foot sometimes dangled.

Scenario5Start.5.full: The Yellow Fever had struck the village, and for several weeks any visit to its somber limits forced the young heirs to keep a cloth handkerchief about their mouth and nostrils to protect from the miasma. While they were remiss to admit it, this seemed the perfect macabre backdrop in which to advance their father's dreadful business.
Scenario5Start.5.easy: Yellow Fever had come to the village. For weeks, the young family had to hold a cloth over their mouth and nose whenever they went there, to protect themselves from the sick air. They did not like to say it, but this dark, deadly place was perfect for their father's terrible business.
Scenario5Start.5.short: Yellow Fever had struck. The heirs kept handkerchiefs pressed to their faces, yet secretly found it the perfect backdrop for their father's dreadful business.

Scenario5Start.6.full: While the prevailing mood in the village was one of morose caution, the young entrepreneurs saw potential in these darkened streets. A particularly ambitious individual could lift this gray village into a thriving city. Perhaps even an aristocrat with coin to spare could make a persuasive argument as to its direction.
Scenario5Start.6.easy: Most people in the village were sad and careful. But the young family saw a chance here. Someone with big plans could turn this gray village into a rich city. And maybe a wealthy noble with money to spend could decide what kind of city it would become.
Scenario5Start.6.short: Where the villagers saw only gloom, the young entrepreneurs saw potential: with ambition and coin, this village could become a thriving city.

Scenario5Start.7.full: As the kindred surveyed the dreary countryside from behind the iron gates of their estate, they watched the billowing mists move slowly across the valley. The townsfolk stirred as a disquieting laugh echoed down from the hillside. They were excited to begin their father's work in earnest!
Scenario5Start.7.easy: From behind the iron gates of their house, the family watched the fog move slowly across the valley. Down in the village, people looked up as a strange laugh came down from the hill. The family could not wait to begin their father's work!
Scenario5Start.7.short: As the mists rolled across the valley, a disquieting laugh echoed from the hillside. They were eager to begin their father's work in earnest!

S5Special1.1.full: **The Town Is in Need of Direction**

S5Special1.2.full: Before resolving this event, all players should complete all start of round actions.

S5Special1.3.full: After the untimely death of the current mayor (and the previous three), the town was once again embroiled in politics. While several mediocre businessmen had thrown their hats into the arena, the family sensed a restlessness in the small village as they searched for direction forward. Having been raised with an affinity for friendly competition, it was decided that governance would be a droll leisure activity for the family. They decided to use their influence to sway the election in their favor.
S5Special1.3.easy: The mayor had died suddenly, just like the three mayors before him, and once again the town was full of politics. Several average businessmen wanted the job, but the family felt that the people of the small village were restless and looking for a new direction. The family had always enjoyed a friendly competition, so they decided that running the town would be a fun hobby. They chose to use their influence to win the election.
S5Special1.3.short: After the mayor's untimely death (and that of the three before him), the restless village needed direction. Fond of friendly competition, the family decided to sway the election in their favor.

S5Special1.4.full: This was especially pressing as the new mayor would immediately **gain 3VP** and then make the decision as to whether to build a **Bank** *(to obtain additional income)*, or to build a **Library** *(to obtain additional knowledge)*.

S5SpecialSetup1.2.full: {0} receives **3VP** immediately. Then, they receive the **Commemorative Mayoral Coin** from the box. And finally, they will choose if they would like to build a Bank or a Library.

S5SpecialSetup1.5.full: For each visit to the Bank, **gain $2.** The Mayor player will also **immediately gain 1VP** for building the Bank.

S5SpecialSetup1.8.full: For each visit to the Library, **gain one Knowledge of your choice** *(not Occult).*

S5SpecialSetup1.9.full: **Which building would the new Mayor like to Build?**

S5Fate1.2.full: Remove all player pieces from the board and Perform the End of a Generation. Return all **Dubious Bartering** cards to the box. Return any remaining {icon:StorybookToken} tokens to the supply.

S5Fate1.3.full: The village of {0} was, for lack of a more appropriate term, agricultural in its funds and like many similar small villages, were woefully unprepared for the ravages of disease. Despite the generosity (or lack thereof) of the family, the church's already severely limited resources have been stretched to their limit in their distinctly unscientific attempts to stem the spread of infection. With no more donations to call upon, the diocese turned to the local financial institutions for aide.
S5Fate1.3.easy: The village of {0} lived mostly from farming. Like many small villages, it was not ready for a terrible disease. The family had given some money, or maybe not much at all. The church had very little money, and it had used almost all of it trying to stop the infection, without any real science. With no more donations coming, the church asked the local banks for help.
S5Fate1.3.short: Poor, rural {0} was unprepared for disease. Its church, exhausted by unscientific efforts against the infection, turned to the local banks for aid.

S5Fate1.4.full: With additional financial capital from the **Bank**, the church obtained the funds needed to build a Hospital.
S5Fate1.4.easy: With extra money from the **Bank**, the church had enough to build a Hospital.
S5Fate1.4.short: With the **Bank**'s money, the church built a Hospital.

S5Fate1.5.full: The addition of a **Library** to the already strained finances of the village proved insurmountable, and the church failed to build a Hospital. Perhaps the lifestyle of an aristocrat blinded the mayor to this reality, but it was certain that the village would progress down a darker path.
S5Fate1.5.easy: The village already had money problems, and building a **Library** was too much for it. The church could not build a Hospital. Maybe the mayor lived too comfortably to see the problem, but one thing was sure: the village would now go down a darker path.
S5Fate1.5.short: The **Library** strained the village's finances too far; the church could not build a Hospital. The village would take a darker path.

S5Fate2.2.full: Remove all player pieces from the board and Perform the End of a Generation. Return all **Dubious Bartering** cards to the box. Return any remaining {icon:StorybookToken} tokens to the supply.

S5Fate2.3.full: The congregation and citizenry, stricken with the weight of those lost in the battle with Yellow Fever, could only provide a meager sum, which placed the financial future of the village into the hands of the most charitable scientists.
S5Fate2.3.easy: The church members and the townspeople were full of grief for everyone who had died of Yellow Fever. They could only give a small amount of money. So the future of the village now depended on the most generous scientists.
S5Fate2.3.short: Grieving their Yellow Fever dead, the townsfolk could give little. The village's future lay with the most charitable scientists.

S5Fate2.5.full: With charitable contributions totaling over **{0}** {icon:S1_HeartToken}, the Hospital was built. The additional medical infrastructure provided the town a respite from another severe outbreak and ushered in a new era.

S5Fate2.8.full: With charitable contributions failing to exceed **{0}** {icon:S1_HeartToken}, the Hospital was not built. This ill-timed news was delivered just as several new cases of influenza spread across the region. Without the Hospital, the results were drastic.

Hospitalintro.3.full: It is said that springtime under the watchful eye of the snow-tipped Carpathian mountains is a wondrous sight to behold. A single excursion in these rolling hills amongst the paths that split green grass is said to reinvigorate the lonely traveler. It is common to catch the aroma of sweet bread in the air, the sounds of babbling streams with moss-covered roots sipping the cool waters, and the richness of golden honey sunsets illuminating the countryside. If but for one season, a certain blitheness, a blissful simplicity of purpose alights the torch of poetry in the dark minds of men.
Hospitalintro.3.easy: People say that spring below the snowy Carpathian mountains is a wonderful sight. A single walk on the paths through the green, rolling hills can give a lonely traveler new energy. You can often smell sweet bread in the air, hear little streams running past mossy roots, and see golden sunsets light up the countryside. For this one season, even dark minds feel happy and simple, and they start to think of poetry.
Hospitalintro.3.short: Spring beneath the snow-tipped Carpathians is a wondrous sight: sweet bread on the air, babbling streams, golden sunsets. For one season, even dark minds turn to poetry.

Hospitalintro.4.full: Therefore, perhaps it is most appropriate that the return of the scientists coincided with this season, as thanks to their predecessors' aid the town had become rejuvenated. The ashen grayness that once dominated the small town had been brightened, like the azalea flowers and crocus that now bloomed in window boxes along the streets.
Hospitalintro.4.easy: So it fits well that the scientists came back in this season. Thanks to the help of their parents' generation, the town had come back to life. The gray ash that once covered the small town was gone, and the town was bright again, like the azalea and crocus flowers now growing in window boxes along the streets.
Hospitalintro.4.short: Fittingly, the scientists returned in spring. Thanks to their predecessors, the ashen town now bloomed like the flowers in its window boxes.

Hospitalintro.5.full: The new hospital had become a site of great hope and strength for the people and the town was able to weather the disease even while the newspapers described the bleakness of the surrounding cities. Due to the work of their progenitors, honorary positions on the board of trustees at the hospital were awarded to their sons and daughters; positions which they sadly could not refuse. However, this controlled proximity to the ravages of disease also offered a boon for scientific inquiries and exploration.
Hospitalintro.5.easy: The new hospital gave the people great hope and strength. The town survived the disease, while the newspapers wrote about how bad things were in the cities nearby. Because of their parents' work, the sons and daughters were given places on the hospital's board of trustees. Sadly, they could not say no. But being so close to the disease was also a great chance for scientific research.
Hospitalintro.5.short: The new hospital gave the town hope while the disease ravaged nearby cities. The heirs inherited seats on its board, which they could not refuse, but the closeness to disease served their science.

Hospitalintro.6.full: This serendipitous push forward in disease prevention attracted the attention of not only the diocese, but also the scientific community hoping to replicate their success. There were even rumors of a government-sponsored university; a prospect that caused great tension within the church and the townsfolk used to their isolated and bucolic existences.
Hospitalintro.6.easy: This lucky success against the disease was noticed by the church, and also by other scientists who wanted to copy it. People even talked about a university paid for by the government. This idea made the church and the townspeople very nervous, because they were used to their quiet, simple life in the countryside.
Hospitalintro.6.short: Their success drew the church and the scientific world. Rumors of a government university unsettled the clergy and the quiet townsfolk.

Hospitalintro.7.full: The possibilities for advancement - and exploitation - seemed limitless. But, would their ingenious and unorthodox ambitions prove too unconventional for the cautious minds of academia? Or would the pressures of rejection from their peers break their indomitable spirit?
Hospitalintro.7.easy: There seemed to be no end to the chances to get ahead, and to use others. But would their clever and unusual plans be too strange for careful scholars? Or would the pain of being rejected by other scientists break their strong spirit?
Hospitalintro.7.short: The possibilities seemed limitless. But would academia reject their unorthodox ambitions, and would rejection break them?

UniversityIntro.3.full: They observed the city from the windows of their manor; watched as men in their brown sack suits and women with sashes tied firmly about their waists wandered the bustling sidewalks and modern pathways that winded throughout the university. What was once a bucolic and unknown region had developed into a thriving metropolis.
UniversityIntro.3.easy: From the windows of their big house, they watched the city. Men in brown suits and women with sashes around their waists walked along the busy sidewalks and the new paths that went all through the university. This quiet, unknown countryside had grown into a large, busy city.
UniversityIntro.3.short: From their manor they watched the bustling university streets. The unknown countryside had become a thriving metropolis.

UniversityIntro.4.full: And yet, it was that very same prosperity of the city that taunted them. Was it not their family's genius, their forebear's business acumen and ambition that exiled disease from the country? Was it not their shrewd antecedents that secured the government's funding of a university — the same who entered into this generation with the secret to eternal life?
UniversityIntro.4.easy: But the city's wealth made them angry. Was it not their family's genius, business skill and ambition that drove the disease out of the country? Was it not their clever parents who got the government to pay for a university, and who began this generation with the secret of eternal life?
UniversityIntro.4.short: Yet the city's prosperity taunted them. Had their family not banished disease, secured the university, and found the secret to eternal life?

UniversityIntro.5.full: Still the townsfolk eyed them as they would a foreigner, with silent judgement in their hearts. While the administration of the university offered assistance and reached out with kind words of encouragement, it was clear to the family that their presence was not truly appreciated. With each passing day, their resentment grew deeper. It seethed under the surface of their ambitious, technical labors.
UniversityIntro.5.easy: But the townspeople still looked at them like strangers and judged them silently. The university's leaders offered help and said kind and encouraging words, but the family knew that people did not really want them there. Every day they became more bitter. This anger grew quietly under all their ambitious technical work.
UniversityIntro.5.short: Still the townsfolk treated them as strangers. Despite the university's kind words, the family felt unwelcome, and their resentment grew.

UniversityIntro.6.full: Science should not be contained by the arbitrary limits of ethics. They believed that this was their chance to legitimize the family's research and to prove that bold, swift, and unmitigatable genius would propel the world forward. The ends would justify the means. From darkness, an electric spark would form to capture the entire scientific world within its grasp!
UniversityIntro.6.easy: They believed that rules about right and wrong should not limit science. This was their chance to show that the family's research was serious, and that bold, fast and unstoppable genius would move the world forward. A good result would make any method acceptable. Out of the darkness, an electric spark would grow and take hold of the whole scientific world!
UniversityIntro.6.short: Ethics should not limit science; the ends would justify the means. From darkness, their spark would seize the scientific world!

NoUniversityIntro.3.full: They arrived by coach on a cold day in autumn, summoned from studies abroad in order to claim an inheritance that, despite their reticence, carried with it an extraordinary wealth that they could not resist. The once bright village they remembered from their eccentric youth was mired in gray fog that clung to the ashen streets. Their carriage nearly unchained itself in the deep muddy ruts of the dilapidated roads nearby.
NoUniversityIntro.3.easy: They came by coach on a cold autumn day. They had been studying in other countries, but they were called home to receive an inheritance. They did not really want it, but it was so rich that they could not say no. They remembered the village as a bright place from their strange childhood, but now it was hidden in a gray fog that hung over the dirty streets. On the broken roads near the village, their carriage almost lost its wheels in the deep mud.
NoUniversityIntro.3.short: They arrived by coach one cold autumn, called home to an inheritance too rich to refuse. The bright village of their youth now lay under gray fog and mud.

NoUniversityIntro.4.full: Not much is written about this time aside from journal entries from the young scientists that all echo an immediate revulsion towards the circumstances in which they found themselves and the sense of despair among the townsfolk. Photographs show us some evidence that the hospital was still in operation but its facilities had fallen into disrepair. The university that had once represented a bastion of new science was reduced to rubble, and in its place a disreputable tavern emerged.
NoUniversityIntro.4.easy: Little was written about this time. There are only the diaries of the young scientists, and they all say how disgusted they were by the situation and how hopeless the townspeople were. Photographs show that the hospital was still open, but its buildings were in bad condition. The university, once a strong home for new science, was now a pile of stones, and in its place stood a tavern with a bad reputation.
NoUniversityIntro.4.short: The young scientists' journals record only revulsion and despair. The hospital was crumbling, and a disreputable tavern stood in the university's ruins.

NoUniversityIntro.5.full: In fact, several public houses had been built upon the main thoroughfare. When the government denied the town a university, the backlash from the peasantry was swift. The citizens developed a sharp distrust of modern advances in science and medicine and were wary of those who displayed signs of intelligence. The grudge they harbored even prevented the extension of the electrical grid to a town in most desperate need of modern updates.
NoUniversityIntro.5.easy: In fact, there were now several pubs on the main street. When the government refused to give the town a university, the poor people reacted quickly and angrily. They stopped trusting modern science and medicine, and they were careful around anyone who seemed too clever. Because of their anger, the town was not even connected to electricity, even though it needed it very badly.
NoUniversityIntro.5.short: Pubs lined the main street. Denied a university, the peasants turned against science and the clever, and even refused electricity.

NoUniversityIntro.6.full: There was an emptiness in the dusty hallways and barren passageways of the ruined Estates and this hollowness pressed upon the cousins' minds most forcefully. For years, they would be forced into secrecy, listless and isolated from their colleagues, their sense of ambition cut short at the most crucial interval. And while a visit to one of the spirited establishments would help quell the masses, the indulgence only made the gravity of the situation wear more heavily upon their features.
NoUniversityIntro.6.easy: The dusty halls and empty corridors of the ruined estates felt very empty, and this emptiness weighed heavily on the cousins. For years they had to work in secret, without energy and far away from other scientists. Their ambition was stopped at the most important moment. A visit to one of the pubs helped to keep the people calm, but drinking only made the cousins look more worried and tired.
NoUniversityIntro.6.short: The empty halls of the ruined Estates weighed on the cousins. For years they worked in secret, isolated, their ambition cut short.

END-WolvesEvil1.2.full: Three generations of diligent scientific minds, toiling at an unspeakable work, surrounded by decaying stone walls, their ignoble experimentations tucked away amongst the deep forests and well-worn dirt roads that traverse the gray countryside.
END-WolvesEvil1.2.easy: Three generations of hard-working scientists did terrible work in old houses with crumbling stone walls. They hid their shameful experiments deep in the forests, along the dirt roads that cross the gray countryside.
END-WolvesEvil1.2.short: Three generations toiled at an unspeakable work, hidden in the forests of the gray countryside.

END-WolvesEvil1.3.full: Could the family's indifference to the plight of the diseased truly be blamed for how the pandemic consumed the region? Is it possible that they assisted a supernatural force that could ingrain themselves so deeply in a small town's infrastructure that an entire populace would be turned into monsters themselves? Or that a counter-agent could be procured and unleashed to undo an evil curse?
END-WolvesEvil1.3.easy: Was it really the family's fault that the disease spread over the whole region, because they did not care about the sick? Could they have helped a supernatural power that grew so deep into a small town that all its people became monsters? Or could someone have made a cure and used it to break an evil curse?
END-WolvesEvil1.3.short: Did the family's indifference let the pandemic consume the region? Did they aid a force that turned a town into monsters, or could a counter-agent undo the curse?

END-WolvesEvil1.4.full: Unearthing this mystery took considerable effort as the history of the region had all but been forgotten and the memory of several eccentric entrepreneurs isolated in aristocratic circles had faded away, obscured by time like the mists that still hang over this small valley. But whether truth or fiction, {0}'s residents cling to these superstitions in whispered conversations. On nights when strange sounds emerged from the fog, they turned their gaze towards the grim chateaus in the distance and wondered what strange machinations were contained within.
END-WolvesEvil1.4.easy: It was hard work to find out the truth. People had almost forgotten the history of the region, and the memory of a few strange business people from rich families had faded with time, like the fog that still hangs over this small valley. True or not, the people of {0} still believe these stories and talk about them in whispers. On nights when strange sounds came out of the fog, they looked at the dark castles in the distance and wondered what strange plans were made inside.
END-WolvesEvil1.4.short: The history is nearly forgotten, faded like the valley's mists. Yet {0}'s residents still whisper of it, and on nights when strange sounds came from the fog, they eyed the grim chateaus and wondered.

END-HuntersEvil1.2.full: The impressive victory over the forces of superstition within the city marked a turning point in the acceptance of scientific experimentation and progress across the entire country. And while their work had done nothing to spare the community from future epidemics, their fears now abated, allowing them to expand deeper into the valley. Lucrative silver mining operations appeared and with it came even more opportunities for the family to invest.
END-HuntersEvil1.2.easy: This great win against superstition in the city changed how the whole country saw scientific experiments and progress. Their work had not protected the town from new diseases, but people were no longer afraid. So they could move further into the valley. Silver mines that made a lot of money were opened, and they gave the family even more chances to invest.
END-HuntersEvil1.2.short: The victory over superstition won the country over to science. Unafraid, the people spread into the valley, and new silver mines gave the family more to invest in.

END-HuntersEvil1.3.full: Tall tales once told to frighten children were now believed to be real, macabre stories of true horrible scientific experiments. And after the hideous experiments let loose were wrangled once again, the respect and fear the people had for the family was demonstrable. For the family, this veneration meant a guarantee of autonomy and resources.
END-HuntersEvil1.3.easy: Old stories that were once told to scare children were now thought to be true: dark stories of real and terrible scientific experiments. After the horrible creatures that had escaped were caught again, it was clear that people both respected and feared the family. For the family, this meant freedom and money for their work.
END-HuntersEvil1.3.short: Old tales to frighten children now seemed true. Once the escaped horrors were caught, the people feared and revered the family, which guaranteed them freedom and resources.

END-HuntersEvil1.4.full: But their fame was merely relegated to the Hungarian hillsides. They had weathered the storm, but now it was time to summon and control the tempest! With their legacy firmly cemented, they stood perched upon the precipice of true scientific discovery, confident and ready for their next moment of brilliance.
END-HuntersEvil1.4.easy: But they were only famous in the Hungarian hills. They had survived the storm, but now it was time to call up the storm and control it! Their place in history was safe, and they were ready for a real scientific discovery, sure of themselves and ready for their next great idea.
END-HuntersEvil1.4.short: But their fame stayed in the Hungarian hills. Now it was time to summon and control the tempest, and to reach for true scientific discovery.

END-WolvesGood1.2.full: There is not much possibility to confirm the notes I have herein on a society of monsters. I have scoured the surviving journal entries, newspaper clippings, and ephemera collected on a visit to the crumbling estates outside of {0}. Or what remains of {1}. Some locals in the areas surrounding the site swear by the stories, but the ensuing decades have made the information scarce and proof even more so.
END-WolvesGood1.2.easy: It is hard to prove what I have written here about a society of monsters. I have searched through the old diaries, newspaper articles and papers that I found when I visited the crumbling estates outside {0}, or what is left of {1}. Some people who live near the place say the stories are true, but many years have passed, so there is little information and even less proof.
END-WolvesGood1.2.short: My notes on a society of monsters are hard to confirm. Journals and clippings from the ruined estates outside {0}, or what remains of {1}, are scarce, and proof scarcer still.

END-WolvesGood1.3.full: The final notes and news clippings available declare that a peace between monster and man finally seemed like an imminent possibility after recent talks with the government. However, it was only weeks later that {0} became yet another casualty of the War to End All Wars. Despite the suspicious distance between the front lines and southeastern Hungary, an evening air raid resulted in a heavy firebomb and phosgene attack that devastated the city, leaving zero known survivors.
END-WolvesGood1.3.easy: The last notes and newspaper articles say that, after talks with the government, peace between monsters and people seemed very close. But only a few weeks later, {0} became one more victim of the Great War. The front line was strangely far away from southeastern Hungary, but one evening an air attack with fire bombs and poison gas destroyed the city. Nobody is known to have survived.
END-WolvesGood1.3.short: Peace between monster and man seemed near. Weeks later, despite its distance from the front, {0} was destroyed by an air raid of firebombs and poison gas. There were no known survivors.

END-WolvesGood1.4.full: As the cousins were vacationing along the Mediterranean at the time, this devastating loss was more one of property and potential opportunity. They were quick to salvage what remained of their experimentations and carry on again in their summer homes. The family had already established a name for themselves across the region, but what they had hoped would change the course of the world would have to wait as it was once again rebuilt.
END-WolvesGood1.4.easy: The cousins were on holiday by the Mediterranean Sea at the time, so for them the loss was mostly about property and missed chances. They quickly saved what was left of their experiments and went on working in their summer houses. The family was already well known in the region, but their dream of changing the world had to wait while it was rebuilt once again.
END-WolvesGood1.4.short: Vacationing on the Mediterranean, the cousins lost only property. They salvaged their experiments and carried on, but changing the world would have to wait.

END-WolvesGood1.5.full: So like the monsters that once attempted to create their own utopian city hidden amongst the rolling hills and forests, the world was not yet ready for the family. But, like a phoenix rising reborn from the embers of destruction, it was assured that they would someday return to shock the world once again.
END-WolvesGood1.5.easy: The monsters had once tried to build their own perfect city, hidden in the hills and forests, and the world had not been ready for them. In the same way, the world was not ready for the family yet. But like a phoenix that rises again from the ashes, they would surely come back one day and shock the world again.
END-WolvesGood1.5.short: Like the monsters and their hidden utopia, the family was too much for the world. But like a phoenix, they would rise again to shock it.

END-HunterGood1.2.full: When disease wreaked havoc across the countryside, they remained safe in isolation, steadfast in their determination to complete a work that would transform our understanding of the world. And when an evil presence burrowed its ghastly business underneath the rebuilding town of {0}, the family ruthlessly exposed their efforts. Their contributions of time and resources to battle away the creatures when they threatened to overtake the countryside shone like a lighthouse in a storm.
END-HunterGood1.2.easy: When disease destroyed lives across the countryside, they stayed safe and alone, determined to finish work that would change how we understand the world. And when an evil power dug its terrible tunnels under {0} while the town was being rebuilt, the family showed everyone what it was doing, without mercy. When the creatures threatened to take over the countryside, the family gave time and money to fight them, and this shone like a lighthouse in a storm.
END-HunterGood1.2.short: Safe in isolation through the epidemic, the family later exposed the evil beneath {0}. Their fight against the creatures shone like a lighthouse in a storm.

END-HunterGood1.3.full: The evil scourge, once a plague of disease and then again a plague of horrors from beyond, had been vanquished, leaving only the knowledge gleaned from their very existence to strengthen the family's pursuits. Though they were unhappy to share the same luminous spotlight with the Fraternity, the fame was grand enough to sate them. The city, the country, and nearly the entirety of Eastern Europe now knew their name.
END-HunterGood1.3.easy: The evil plague, first a plague of disease and then a plague of horrors from another world, was defeated. All that was left was what they had learned from it, and this made the family's work stronger. They did not like sharing the fame with the Fraternity, but there was enough fame for them to be happy. The city, the country and almost all of Eastern Europe now knew their name.
END-HunterGood1.3.short: The scourge of disease and horrors was vanquished, and its lessons fed the family's work. They shared the spotlight with the Fraternity, but all of Eastern Europe knew their name.

END-HunterGood1.4.full: It was a time of peace, but not a time of rest. They had so much more science to explore and so many new generations to do it. The world would soon quiver at the very mention of that family!
END-HunterGood1.4.easy: It was a time of peace, but not a time to rest. There was so much more science to explore, and many new generations to do it. Soon the world would shake just at the name of that family!
END-HunterGood1.4.short: Peace, but no rest: more science awaited. The world would soon quiver at that family's name!

The research required for his later notes was known to have exacerbated his dipsomania. His untimely exit remains a stark reminder of the perils of inebriation.
END-NoUniGood.2.easy: This book is dedicated to Dr. Ensign Benwallis. He leaves behind two children, his daughter Celia Benwallis Cartwright and his son Ensign Benwallis Jr. With a heavy heart, we know that his story ends somewhere in these pages, but we want his words to live on. The research for his later notes made his drinking problem worse. His early death is a clear warning about the dangers of alcohol.
END-NoUniGood.2.short: Dedicated to Dr. Ensign Benwallis, survived by his children Celia Benwallis Cartwright and Ensign Benwallis Jr. His research worsened his drinking, and his untimely death warns of its perils.

END-NoUniGood.7.short: Hungary's poor schooling and missing electricity bar further publication there, but we hope other European readers will enjoy it.

END-NoUniGood.8.easy: The strange and famous scientific work of the family will surely be remembered for many years.

S5Specialbar1.2.full: While the cousins thrived in the lamplit tenebrosity of their basement laboratories and spent many evenings observing the melancholic, ashen mists that enveloped the nearby village, the lack of modern convenience - of light and electricity which had been granted across all of Europe - had become a detriment to their experimental capabilities.
S5Specialbar1.2.easy: The cousins loved working in their dark basement laboratories by lamplight, and on many evenings they watched the sad, gray fog that covered the village nearby. But the village had no modern comforts, no electric light and no electricity, even though the rest of Europe had them. This now made their experiments harder.
S5Specialbar1.2.short: The cousins loved their lamplit basement laboratories, but the village's lack of electricity, enjoyed across Europe, now hampered their experiments.

S5Specialbar1.3.full: One particularly chill evening in winter, a meeting was called at the Town Hall, in which the topic of electricity and connection to the national grid was reintroduced. However, possibly fueled by many in attendance having already given patronage to the local pub, the icy mood of the meeting suddenly erupted into a fiery debate. The meeting soon descended into chaos and was adjourned as a minor brawl spilled out into the snow-covered streets. It appeared as if nothing would be done without intervention.
S5Specialbar1.3.easy: On one very cold winter evening, there was a meeting at the Town Hall about electricity and connecting the town to the national power network. Many people had already visited the local pub before the meeting. The cold mood suddenly turned into a hot argument. The meeting became chaos and was ended when a small fight moved out into the snowy streets. It seemed that nothing would happen unless someone stepped in.
S5Specialbar1.3.short: A winter meeting at the Town Hall about electricity, fueled by the local pub, ended in a brawl in the snowy streets. Nothing would happen without intervention.

S5Specialbar1.4.full: With their influence amongst aristocratic circles, it would only take a minute amount of effort for the cousins to levy outside approval for the installation of an electrical grid. But were they aligned in their desire to agitate the masses?
S5Specialbar1.4.easy: The cousins had influence with rich and powerful people, so it would be easy for them to get approval from outside for an electrical network. But did they all want to stir up the people?
S5Specialbar1.4.short: Their aristocratic friends could easily secure an electrical grid. But did the cousins agree on stirring up the masses?

ForScience.3.full: For a normal scientist, it should be the pinnacle of achievements; an honor that would ensure their name etched forever in the halls of academia. And that was just it. To be revered fondly by the same association that simultaneously despises the very source of the family's infamous ingenuity. Not to mention the additional obligations from the cursed establishment would pull them from their work up until their final hours.

HubertusWolves1.3.full: I, {0}, am writing this letter to you after my meeting with an associate of the International Order of St. Hubertus. Our conversation was brief, but the resulting knowledge has piqued my curiosities.
HubertusWolves1.3.easy: I, {0}, am writing to you after I met a member of the International Order of St. Hubertus. We did not talk for long, but what I learned has made me very curious.
HubertusWolves1.3.short: I, {0}, write after a brief meeting with a member of the International Order of St. Hubertus that piqued my curiosity.

HubertusWolves1.4.full: It has been revealed to me that your intentions are

HubertusWolves1.5.full: nefarious. The malevolent Order is consumed with greed, seeking to unearth the ancient secrets in this area and use this power to alter humanity and spread a plague of monstrous entities across the world. You only asked for your work to remain **concealed**.
HubertusWolves1.5.easy: evil. The wicked Order is full of greed. It wants to dig up the old secrets of this area and use their power to change humanity and spread a plague of monsters across the world. You only asked me to keep your work **concealed**.
HubertusWolves1.5.short: nefarious. The greedy Order seeks this area's ancient secrets, to alter humanity and spread monsters across the world. You only asked for your work to stay **concealed**.

HubertusWolves1.6.full: demonstrably positive. The Order is only concerned with establishing a safe haven for those afflicted by disease. Your representative even revealed a physical peculiarity that had elongated her cuspids into sharp points. She left swiftly before nightfall, ignoring my pleas for her to remain, but she urged me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to become apparent.
HubertusWolves1.6.easy: clearly good. The Order only wants to build a safe place for people who suffer from disease. Your messenger even showed me something strange about her body: her canine teeth had grown into sharp points. She left quickly before dark, even though I begged her to stay, but she told me to **investigate** the secret work that would soon come to light.
HubertusWolves1.6.short: demonstrably positive. The Order seeks only a safe haven for the diseased. Your envoy, her canines grown into sharp points, left before nightfall, urging me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to surface.

HubertusWolves1.7.full: Being intimately familiar with matters of the occult, this admission is unsurprising. My apprehensions are only related to how your actions will impact my ability to advance my scientific studies most generously.
HubertusWolves1.7.easy: I know the world of the occult very well, so this news does not surprise me. I am only worried about how your actions will affect my own scientific work.
HubertusWolves1.7.short: Versed in the occult, I am unsurprised. I only worry how your actions will affect my research.

CureMoonSick1.2.full: What a horrible night to have a curse!

CureMoonSick1.3.full: They wrote of torn clothing, strange awakenings half-naked in the gardens at the edge of their Estate, of blood speckled about their boots and dried streaks from the corners of their lips. Lingering lucid memories of stalking prey in the woods haunted their dreams yet filled them with a terrible energy!
CureMoonSick1.3.easy: They wrote about torn clothes, and about waking up half-naked in the gardens at the edge of their Estate, with drops of blood on their boots and dried blood at the corners of their mouths. Clear memories of hunting animals in the woods haunted their dreams, but they also filled them with a terrible energy!
CureMoonSick1.3.short: They wrote of torn clothes, waking half-naked in the gardens with blood on their boots and lips. Memories of stalking prey haunted their dreams, yet filled them with terrible energy!

CureMoonSick1.4.full: When they discovered the eviscerated body of one of their servants skewered upon the metal fence that lined the grounds, the bestial teeth and claw marks told a new story. They steeled their mind against the distraction, recommitting themselves with deadly focus to the task at hand.
CureMoonSick1.4.easy: Then they found the body of one of their servants, torn open and stuck on the metal fence around the grounds. The marks of animal teeth and claws told a new story. They did not let this distract them, and they went back to their work with deadly focus.
CureMoonSick1.4.short: A servant's mauled body on the estate fence, with bestial teeth and claw marks, told a new story. They steeled themselves and returned to work.

CureMoonSick1.5.full: They could not dwell on the news of yet another victim within their household for long as more pressing matters of scientific import weighed upon their every waking hour.
CureMoonSick1.5.easy: They could not think for long about another victim in their house, because more important scientific work filled every hour they were awake.
CureMoonSick1.5.short: Another victim in the household, but more pressing science awaited.

CureMoonSick1.6.full: For theirs was a dismal, macabre occupation. They measured each moment in dark pen strokes, the incision of a sterilized blade, or the ebullition of glowing liquid in a graduated flask. The loss of a servant was unfortunate, not for the life it represented, but for the distinct lapse in efficiency procuring a new servant would cause.
CureMoonSick1.6.easy: Their work was dark and gloomy. They counted every moment in black pen marks, in the cut of a clean knife, or in the bubbling of a glowing liquid in a glass flask. Losing a servant was a pity, not because a life was lost, but because finding a new servant would slow down their work.
CureMoonSick1.6.short: Theirs was a macabre work of pen, scalpel and glowing flask. A servant's loss mattered only for the time it took to find another.

bar1.3.full: After a brief excursion to the local pub, I happened to engage in a spirited conversation with the **Blacksmith’s** son. Being slightly out of my wits, his slightly improper offer to accompany him home to his chateau for further libations appealed. We engaged in a delightful conversation, so intriguing in fact, that I accepted his generous offer of temporary lodging for the evening. I will spare the details of our respectable and entirely benign conversation.
bar1.3.easy: After a short visit to the local pub, I had a lively conversation with the **Blacksmith’s** son. I was a little drunk, so I liked his slightly improper offer to come to his home for more drinks. Our conversation was so interesting that I accepted his kind offer to stay the night. I will not describe our respectable and completely harmless conversation.
bar1.3.short: After the pub, a lively talk with the **Blacksmith’s** son led to his offer of more drinks and lodging for the night. I will spare the details of our entirely respectable conversation.

bar1.4.full: We both decided to disrobe as any person would when making nightly preparations for sleep. Regrettably, though I cannot recollect how it occurred, the Blacksmith was unpleased to discover us similarly nude and entwined in this state the next morning, surrounded by several defiled tools from the forge. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the Blacksmith and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar1.4.easy: We both took off our clothes, as anyone would before going to sleep. Sadly, and I cannot remember how it happened, the next morning the Blacksmith was not happy to find us both naked and wrapped around each other, surrounded by several dirty tools from the forge. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the Blacksmith, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar1.4.short: The Blacksmith was displeased to find us nude and entwined the next morning among his defiled tools. Our family's reputation was sullied at the Blacksmith and I resolved to avoid it.

bar1.5.full: After a brief excursion to the local pub, I happened to engage in a spirited conversation with the **Blacksmith’s** daughter. While I am unable to discern the reasoning behind my actions, I have since apologized for my repeated comments besmirching her virtuous nature; comments which apparently resulted in a minor altercation with a gentlemen or two at the fine establishment.
bar1.5.easy: After a short visit to the local pub, I had a lively conversation with the **Blacksmith’s** daughter. I cannot understand why I did it, but I have since said sorry for my many comments that insulted her good name. These comments seem to have led to a small fight with a gentleman or two at that fine pub.
bar1.5.short: At the pub I talked with the **Blacksmith’s** daughter. I have since apologized for repeatedly insulting her virtue, which apparently led to a brawl or two.

bar1.6.full: It was around midnight that I decided to make a quiet exit, in order to properly avoid any further antagonism. My clothes, soiled and bloodied by the ensuing brawl, were found discarded along the muddy trek to the Blacksmith's forge. While I have no recollection of the ensuing events, multiple witnesses attest that I then proceeded to brand the blacksmith's dog and passed out naked in the slack tub. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the Blacksmith and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar1.6.easy: Around midnight I decided to leave quietly, so that there would be no more trouble. My clothes, dirty and bloody from the fight, were found on the muddy path to the Blacksmith's forge. I remember nothing of what happened next, but several people say that I branded the blacksmith's dog and then fell asleep naked in the water tub. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the Blacksmith, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar1.6.short: My bloodied clothes were found on the path to the forge. Witnesses say I branded the blacksmith's dog and passed out naked in the slack tub. Our family's reputation was sullied at the Blacksmith and I resolved to avoid it.

bar1.7.full: Place a {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Blacksmith**. When a player takes an action at this location, they **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** for every {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on that location.

bar2.3.full: While many first-hand accounts from the townsfolk may not corroborate my story, I cannot conceal my disgust with the insinuation. The stable hand and I were simply enjoying a midnight ride in the nearby beet fields in the spirit of the season. Due to my enhanced state of inebriation, I may have chosen the incorrect steed for our excursion.
bar2.3.easy: Many townspeople tell a different story, but I must say how disgusted I am by what they suggest. The stable boy and I were only enjoying a midnight ride in the beet fields nearby, in the spirit of the season. Because I was very drunk, I may have chosen the wrong animal for our ride.
bar2.3.short: Whatever the townsfolk say, the stable hand and I merely took a midnight ride through the beet fields. Being very drunk, I may have chosen the wrong steed.

bar2.4.full: I awoke in the stables beside my porcine companion, who had been outfitted with a leather riding saddle. The gate to their pen had been left open and the entire pig population of the town was scattered throughout the streets.
bar2.4.easy: I woke up in the stables next to my pig friend, who was wearing a leather riding saddle. The gate of the pig pen had been left open, and all the pigs of the town were running around in the streets.
bar2.4.short: I awoke beside a saddled pig. The pen stood open and the town's pigs roamed the streets.

bar2.5.full: I would also like to note that the charges of public nudity against me are warrantless, as upon discovery of my predicament that morning, I hastily endeavored to hide my shame and purchase new clothing from a local tailor as would be customary in such a situation. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Farmer’s Market** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar2.5.easy: I would also like to say that the charges of being naked in public are unfair. When I found myself in this situation that morning, I quickly tried to cover myself and buy new clothes from a local tailor, as anyone would do. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Farmer’s Market**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar2.5.short: The public nudity charge is unfounded: I hurried to a tailor at once. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Farmer’s Market** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar2.6.full: I find the accusations toward my conduct and character most disturbing. To insinuate that I was openly consorting with individuals of ill-repute and offered compensation for illicit activities, why it is as absurd as the other charges against me from that evening.
bar2.6.easy: I find the accusations about my behavior and character very upsetting. To suggest that I openly spent time with people of bad reputation and offered them money for forbidden activities is as ridiculous as the other charges against me from that evening.
bar2.6.short: That I consorted with disreputable people and paid for illicit favors is as absurd as the other charges.

bar2.7.full: While I admit to having a few additional libations, it is most presumptuous to believe that just because I was found near the open door of my carriage in the buff, covered in tomato paste, with lipstick impressions across the entirety of my form, that I would be held responsible for the debasing of a bushel of cherry tomatoes and several other vegetable stocks.
bar2.7.easy: I admit that I had a few more drinks. But it is wrong to think that I am responsible for ruining a basket of cherry tomatoes and several other vegetables, just because I was found naked near the open door of my carriage, covered in tomato paste, with lipstick marks all over my body.
bar2.7.short: Being found naked by my carriage, covered in tomato paste and lipstick, hardly proves I defiled a bushel of cherry tomatoes.

bar2.8.full: Despite my personal objections, I have summarily reimbursed the stall owner for their produce and discretion in the matter. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Farmer’s Market** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar2.8.easy: Although I do not agree, I have paid the stall owner for their vegetables and for keeping quiet about it. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Farmer’s Market**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar2.8.short: I have nonetheless paid the stall owner for produce and discretion. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Farmer’s Market** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar3.3.full: It was very much in poor taste for a **fortune teller** to summarily dismiss my romantic advances given my current social status and level of wealth. However, I admit that my inebriated reaction to steal and destroy her Tarot deck was highly juvenile. And the public defiling of said Tarot cards afterwards was certainly not in keeping with the standards of my aristocratic upbringing.
bar3.3.easy: It was very rude of a **fortune teller** to say no to my romantic advances, because I am rich and important. But I admit that stealing and destroying her Tarot cards while I was drunk was very childish. And what I did to those Tarot cards in public afterwards was certainly not how an aristocrat should behave.
bar3.3.short: The **fortune teller** rudely rejected my advances. Drunkenly stealing and publicly defiling her Tarot deck was, I admit, juvenile.

bar3.4.full: I have since reimbursed the Fortune Teller for her ruined Tarot cards, and apologized to the Sheriff for my display of public nudity. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the Fortune Teller and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar3.4.easy: I have paid the Fortune Teller for her ruined Tarot cards, and I have said sorry to the Sheriff for being naked in public. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the Fortune Teller, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar3.4.short: I have repaid the Fortune Teller and apologized to the Sheriff for my nudity. Our family's reputation was sullied at the Fortune Teller and I resolved to avoid it.

bar3.5.full: During a spirited conversation at the local pub, I was informed of a fine establishment with premium snuff and tobacco on the outskirts of town. While I cannot recall if I partook, I was made aware that this establishment promoted opium use, which is a vile indulgence indeed. Sadly, I admit poor judgement in not exiting the premises immediately upon this discovery and my subsequent refusal to leave after four hours had elapsed.
bar3.5.easy: During a lively conversation at the local pub, someone told me about a fine shop at the edge of town with excellent snuff and tobacco. I cannot remember if I tried any, but I learned that this place offered opium, which is a terrible habit. Sadly, I made a bad choice: I did not leave at once when I found this out, and I still refused to leave after four hours.
bar3.5.short: I visited an establishment outside town that turned out to offer opium. I did not leave at once, and still refused after four hours.

bar3.6.full: An exchange of bitter words may have occurred, which resulted in myself yelling expletives and unfortunate ethnic slurs which I would dare not repeat. At some point my clothes had vanished, so I was at a distinct physical disadvantage when I was swiftly removed from the area, not without sustaining several bruises from the scuffle (which, to note, I have not pressed charges for). Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Fortune Teller** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar3.6.easy: There may have been an angry argument, and I shouted rude words and ugly insults that I will not repeat. At some point my clothes had disappeared, so I could not defend myself well when I was quickly thrown out, and I got several bruises in the fight (for which, I should say, I have not gone to court). Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Fortune Teller**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar3.6.short: Insults were exchanged, my clothes vanished, and I was removed, bruised. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Fortune Teller** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar4.3.full: The celebration had been exceedingly rowdy. I could not recall whose birthday or anniversary was being celebrated, but I could remember my celebratory stilted walk to the **General Store** near midnight. In my admittedly intoxicated state, I required sustenance.
bar4.3.easy: The party had been very loud and wild. I could not remember whose birthday or anniversary it was, but I remember my happy, stiff walk to the **General Store** around midnight. I was drunk, I admit, and I needed food.
bar4.3.short: After a rowdy celebration, I staggered drunk and hungry to the **General Store** near midnight.

bar4.4.full: Unfortunately, my hunger pangs may have overtaken my sensibilities. A rock may have been plunged through the front window, and I may have been discovered the next morning by the constabulary, passed out naked on the wooden floor, surrounded by several empty cartons of canned sardines, the contents of which may have been returned to the same general area in a more semi-digested form. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the General Store and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar4.4.easy: Sadly, my hunger may have been stronger than my good sense. A rock may have gone through the front window. And the next morning the police may have found me asleep and naked on the wooden floor, among several empty boxes of sardines, whose contents may have come back out again, half-digested, in the same place. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the General Store, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar4.4.short: A rock may have breached the window, and the constabulary may have found me naked among empty sardine tins, some contents returned semi-digested. Our family's reputation was sullied at the General Store and I resolved to avoid it.

bar4.5.full: The proprietors of the General Store, Hagen and Mabel Varga, are respectable, upstanding citizens of whom I have a deep respect. Their fine emporium of quality products is a grand example of successful private business ownership that positively serves the community.
bar4.5.easy: The owners of the General Store, Hagen and Mabel Varga, are respectable, honest citizens, and I respect them very much. Their fine shop of quality products is a great example of a successful private business that helps the community.
bar4.5.short: Hagen and Mabel Varga, owners of the General Store, are upstanding citizens whose fine emporium serves the community well.

bar4.6.full: My unfortunate public statements to the contrary in a loud and admittedly inebriated state were categorically untrue and misinformed. My subsequent scrawling of expletives upon their business' front window - with a crude writing medium that I will not elaborate upon - was brash and reckless.
bar4.6.easy: What I said in public about them, loudly and while drunk, was completely untrue and wrong. Afterwards I wrote rude words on their shop window, with a writing material that I will not describe, and this was rash and careless.
bar4.6.short: My loud, drunken claims otherwise were untrue, and scrawling expletives on their window, in a medium I will not name, was reckless.

bar4.7.full: I regret that my nude form was discovered curled up at their doorstep by the constabulary. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the General Store and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar4.7.easy: I am sorry that the police found me naked and curled up on their doorstep. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the General Store, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar4.7.short: I regret being found naked on their doorstep. Our family's reputation was sullied at the General Store and I resolved to avoid it.

bar4.8.full: Place a {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **General Store**. When a player takes an action at this location, they **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** for every {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on that location.

bar5.3.full: I vaguely remember the phrase that began the argument, but the stitches above my left eye from a shattered glass mug jogged my recollection of the ensuing brawl. A quick nightcap turned into an extended stay of tumbled barstools, belligerence, and wild accusations. My injuries must have been extensive as my memory ceased soon after.
bar5.3.easy: I only partly remember the words that started the argument, but the stitches above my left eye, from a broken glass mug, helped me remember the fight that followed. One quick drink before bed turned into a long night of falling barstools, aggression and wild accusations. I must have been badly hurt, because I remember nothing after that.
bar5.3.short: I barely recall what started it, but the stitches from a shattered mug recall the brawl. A nightcap became a night of tumbled barstools and accusations, and then nothing.

bar5.4.full: My displeased spouse informed me that I was currently the height of gossip within the town. First-hand accounts - of which I cannot confirm given my state of awareness - described how I spat blood in a nurse’s face, tore off my leggings (and undergarments), tried to punch the vicar thrice, and defiled myself in the lobby. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Hospital** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar5.4.easy: My unhappy spouse told me that the whole town was talking about me. People who were there say (I cannot confirm it, as I was not fully awake) that I spat blood in a nurse's face, tore off my trousers (and my underwear), tried to punch the priest three times and soiled myself in the waiting room. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Hospital**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar5.4.short: I was the town's gossip: I reportedly spat blood at a nurse, stripped, swung at the vicar thrice and soiled myself in the lobby. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Hospital** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar5.5.full: I should not have attempted to perform a surgical procedure in my state. Nor should I have locked myself in the surgical arena with a patient, barred the door, and undressed, dousing myself in a carbolic acid solution for the purposes of sterilization. However, my honor had been questioned at the pub and I deemed it only necessary to demonstrate my surgical prowess.
bar5.5.easy: I should not have tried to do an operation in my condition. And I should not have locked myself in the operating room with a patient, blocked the door, taken off my clothes and poured an acid cleaning liquid over myself to make myself clean. But someone at the pub had questioned my honor, and I thought I had to show my skill as a surgeon.
bar5.5.short: I should not have operated in my state, nor locked myself in with a patient, undressed and doused myself in carbolic acid. But my honor had been questioned at the pub.

bar5.6.full: The demonstration of my experimentation capabilities - which are normally formidable, I might add - turned into a series of unfortunate mishaps and misunderstandings. The unfortunate patient has since made a full recovery and has already received a generous stipend in recompense and the hospital a donation with which to cleanse the arena of the admittedly large quantity of blood on the walls, seating, instruments, and ceiling. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Hospital** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar5.6.easy: My demonstration of my skills, which are usually excellent, I might add, turned into a series of unlucky accidents and misunderstandings. The poor patient is completely healthy again and has been paid a generous sum. The hospital also received a donation to clean the operating room, because there was, I admit, a lot of blood on the walls, the seats, the instruments and the ceiling. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Hospital**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar5.6.short: The demonstration went awry. The patient has recovered and been compensated, and the hospital paid to clean the blood from walls, seats, instruments and ceiling. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Hospital** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar5.7.full: Place a {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Hospital**. When a player takes an action at this location, they **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** for every {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on that location.

bar6.3.full: Although witnesses claim that I had carried a makeshift torch several blocks to the destination, my ignition of nearby gasoline reserves was entirely accidental. My intent, of course, was a comical reenactment of the wiles of recent angry mobs; clearly satirical in nature. A vaudevillian parody. However, the French performance art overtones due to my regrettable nudity were not considered with high regard. The resulting blaze that consumed over half of the Laborer’s Union building that night was also not met with the warmest of receptions.
bar6.3.easy: People say that I carried a homemade torch for several streets, but setting fire to the petrol stored nearby was a complete accident. Of course, I only wanted to make a funny copy of the angry crowds we had seen lately, clearly as a joke. A comic show. But people did not like the artistic French touch of my, sadly, naked body. And they also did not like the fire that burned down more than half of the Laborer’s Union building that night.
bar6.3.short: I did carry a torch there, but igniting the gasoline was an accident; I meant only a naked parody of the angry mobs. The blaze that took half the Laborer’s Union building was poorly received.

bar6.4.full: Honestly, the Laborer’s Union building had not been updated for years. It was overdue for renovations. However, our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Laborer’s Union** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar6.4.easy: To be honest, the Laborer’s Union building had not been modernized for years. It needed repairs anyway. But our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Laborer’s Union**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar6.4.short: The building was overdue for renovation anyway. But our family's reputation was sullied at the **Laborer’s Union** and I resolved to avoid it.

bar6.5.full: Place a {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Laborer's Union**. When a player takes an action at this location, they **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** for every {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on that location.

bar7.3.full: While the cemetery has certainly been a crucial source of ingredients for my experiments - acquired by pruning local flora and herbs - calling attention to this fact very loudly while inside the local pub was probably a mistake. Openly inviting all patrons to join me in the cemetery to kick over headstones and then running directly to said location to do so was a clear error of judgement. My alleged indecent exposure whilst doing so, also unfortunate.
bar7.3.easy: The cemetery is certainly an important source of ingredients for my experiments, which I get by picking local plants and herbs. bar7.3.short: Loudly announcing at the pub that the cemetery supplies my ingredients, then leading everyone there to kick over headstones, was an error, as was my alleged nudity.

bar7.4.full: After being treated for a sprained ankle, I spent a night half-remembered in the local police station. Our family’s reputation was certainly sullied at the **Cemetery** and I resolved to avoid it in the future.
bar7.4.easy: After a doctor treated my twisted ankle, I spent a night that I only half remember at the local police station. Our family's name was certainly damaged at the **Cemetery**, and I decided to stay away from it in the future.
bar7.4.short: A sprained ankle and a night in the police station followed. Our family's reputation was sullied at the **Cemetery** and I resolved to avoid it.

Panacea.2.full: It seemed that finally, after years of tireless dedication, a solution to the ails of all men had been formulated. The family was divided on the efficacy of this course of action, but one individual forged ahead recklessly, headless to their warnings.
Panacea.2.easy: It seemed that at last, after years of hard work, they had found a medicine against all human illnesses. The family did not agree on whether this plan would work, but one of them went ahead carelessly and did not listen to their warnings.
Panacea.2.short: After years of work, a cure for all ills seemed at hand. The family was divided, but one of them forged ahead recklessly.

Panacea1.2.full: In a shocking display of altruism, the findings were published in a series of medical journals at the behest of the university's administration. The published work was controversial, but considered revolutionary, as the strength of the failed **Panacea** had several alternative applications.
Panacea1.2.easy: Surprisingly unselfishly, the results were published in a series of medical journals, because the university's leaders asked for it. The work was controversial, but people thought it was revolutionary, because the power of the failed **Panacea** could be used in several other ways.
Panacea1.2.short: At the university's request, the findings were published: controversial but revolutionary, since the failed **Panacea** had other uses.

Panacea1.3.full: The local population, while grateful for the additional tourism, were less than consoled. As much as it was innovative, it was also a secretly manufactured chemical so devastating that all organic matter deteriorated within minutes of it's application.
Panacea1.3.easy: The local people were happy about the extra tourists, but they did not feel much better. The invention was new and clever, but it was also a secretly made chemical so destructive that all living material fell apart within minutes after it was used.
Panacea1.3.short: The locals welcomed the tourists but not the chemical: it destroyed all organic matter within minutes.

PanaceaTooOld.2.full: With only a few years left in their existence, and hence the existence of their familial rivals, {0} realized that it was too late for their creation to have a critical effect on their endeavors.
PanaceaTooOld.2.easy: {0} had only a few years left to live, and so had their family rivals. They realized that it was too late for their invention to really help their plans.
PanaceaTooOld.2.short: With only a few years left, {0} realized it was too late for their creation to matter.

PanaceaTooOld.3.full: This crucial realization was certainly prompted by the entire reserves of the concoction being exhausted one evening when testing the local livestock. Ah, how the mind fades with old age!
PanaceaTooOld.3.easy: They realized this mostly because, one evening, they used up all of the mixture while testing it on the local farm animals. Oh, how the mind gets weaker with age!
PanaceaTooOld.3.short: Not least because they used it all up one evening on the local livestock. Ah, old age!

PanaceaUnleash.3.full: It was a fine summer morning when I heard a piercing scream from the garden. While I had grown relatively accustomed to this cry of distress in my experimentations, it was decidedly peculiar to hear the sound over morning coffee and crepes.
PanaceaUnleash.3.easy: It was a beautiful summer morning when I heard a loud scream from the garden. I was quite used to cries like this from my experiments, but it was very strange to hear one during morning coffee and pancakes.
PanaceaUnleash.3.short: One summer morning, a scream came from the garden: familiar from my experiments, but odd over coffee and crepes.

PanaceaUnleash.4.full: After sashing my robe about me, I exited the manor in time to witness the final moments of a servant tending to the trimming. With a quick lurch, they turned towards me, now beyond sound as their facial features collapsed inwardly. Sanguine chunks of flesh fell to the ground and sizzled like bacon grease on the grass. Within seconds, the human figure that once tended to our garden was a sloshy pile of pink and white froth on the lawn and whatever substance had caused it had seeped deep into the ground, creating a considerable hole in the landscaping.
PanaceaUnleash.4.easy: I tied my robe and went out of the house just in time to see the last moments of a servant who was cutting the hedges. They suddenly turned towards me, but could no longer make a sound, as their face fell in on itself. Bloody pieces of flesh fell to the ground and hissed on the grass like hot bacon fat. Within seconds, the person who had looked after our garden was a wet pile of pink and white foam on the lawn. Whatever had caused it had soaked deep into the ground and left a large hole in the garden.
PanaceaUnleash.4.short: Outside, I saw a servant's face collapse inward. Flesh sizzled on the grass, and within seconds they were a pile of pink froth, the substance eating a hole deep into the lawn.

PanaceaUnleash.5.full: I took a sip of coffee and examined a nearby glass vial labeled as "vital elixir for use in the prevention of disease." I recognized our dear cousin's penmanship instantly; the prankster!
PanaceaUnleash.5.easy: I drank some coffee and looked at a small glass bottle nearby with the label "vital elixir for use in the prevention of disease." I knew the handwriting at once: it was our dear cousin's. What a joker!
PanaceaUnleash.5.short: Sipping my coffee, I found a vial labeled "vital elixir for use in the prevention of disease" in our dear cousin's hand. The prankster!

PanaceaUnleash.6.full: However, unfortunately, another servant stood slack-jawed near the gate, having witnessed the entire spectacle. It would be difficult to replace this worker.
PanaceaUnleash.6.easy: Sadly, another servant was standing near the gate with an open mouth. They had seen everything. It would be hard to replace this worker.
PanaceaUnleash.6.short: Sadly, another servant at the gate had seen it all. They would be hard to replace.

SymposiumEvent3.2.short: The audience was astonished; some of the weaker-willed fainted, clearly overwhelmed by such visionary experiments.

LosingOrderAid.2.full: It was during a period of adjustment to their new surroundings that customary preparations were made to redecorate the west wing of the manor in a more modern style to which they were accustomed. Expecting a delivery of druggets from a Persian carpeter, instead they were greeted by a strapping young man in a burgundy leather coat. He tipped his wide-brimmed hat solemnly.
LosingOrderAid.2.easy: While they were getting used to their new home, they made the usual plans to decorate the west wing of the house in the more modern style they liked. They were waiting for some carpets from a Persian carpet maker, but instead a strong young man in a dark red leather coat came to the door. He seriously lifted his wide hat to greet them.
LosingOrderAid.2.short: Awaiting Persian carpets for the west wing, they were instead greeted by a strapping young man in a burgundy leather coat, who solemnly tipped his hat.

LosingOrderAid.3.full: "Your family has made a contribution to our Fraternity and we are here to repay that debt through service," the young man stated, pulling back his shirt sleeve to reveal a tattoo of a bow and arrow. He then exited to the servant's quarters without further instruction.
LosingOrderAid.3.easy: "Your family has given something to our Fraternity, and we are here to pay back that debt with our service," said the young man. He pulled back his shirt sleeve and showed a tattoo of a bow and arrow. Then he went to the servants' rooms without waiting for orders.
LosingOrderAid.3.short: "Your family has contributed to our Fraternity, and we repay that debt through service," he said, baring a bow-and-arrow tattoo, and went to the servants' quarters.
