FeverServe1.2.full: The small village certainly offered a degree of seclusion and a minute amount of rustic charm on the days when gangrenous bodies of the afflicted were not carted through the streets. But in accordance with this anonymity, it did not easily provide the luxuries generally afforded to the whims of {0} young aristocrats and their spouses.
FeverServe1.2.easy: The small village was certainly quiet and private, and it had a little country charm on the days when the rotting bodies of the sick were not carried through the streets. But because it was so far from everything, it did not offer the luxuries that {0} young aristocrats and their spouses usually expected.
FeverServe1.2.short: The village offered seclusion, and some rustic charm when no gangrenous bodies were carted past, but few luxuries for {0} young aristocrats and their spouses.

FeverServe1.3.full: The family was overjoyed then to receive a letter from some of their most trusted colleagues; however, this joy abated when they detailed an opportunity to offer wardship and tutelage to unfortunate youths failing in their studies. While the interruption was exasperating, an additional hand would allow them more time to focus on important work and to avoid the aromas of the local peasantry.
FeverServe1.3.easy: So the family was very happy when they got a letter from some of their most trusted colleagues. But they were less happy when they read that they were asked to take care of and teach some unlucky young people who were failing at school. It was an annoying disturbance, but an extra helper would give them more time for their important work, and to stay away from the smells of the local peasants.
FeverServe1.3.short: A letter from trusted colleagues asked them to take in failing students. Exasperating, but an extra hand meant more time for work, and less of the peasants' aromas.

FeverServe1.4.full: Each player **pays $1 and gains a SERVANT from LOST** and places it in their Quarters.

FeverServe2.2.full: During the heat of summer, a handsomely dressed woman arrived at each estate with a letter in hand. Interestingly, a former business associate of their mother's requested a daughter be put under each of the houses' charge; along with a considerable stipend to offset the cost. While an appreciable burden, it was irrefusable given the social mores of the time. Being twenty-three and therefore past the age of reasonable marriage, she accepted the new labors with a somewhat heavy heart and was quickly ingratiated into the fold.
FeverServe2.2.easy: In the heat of summer, a well-dressed woman came to each estate with a letter. Interestingly, an old business partner of their mother asked each house to take care of a daughter, and offered a large sum of money to pay for it. It was quite a burden, but in those times you could not say no. She was twenty-three, so too old to marry easily, and she began her new work with a heavy heart, but quickly became part of the family.
FeverServe2.2.short: In summer, a well-dressed woman brought each estate a letter: their mother's former associate asked them to take in a daughter, with a generous stipend. Social custom made it irrefusable. At twenty-three and past marrying age, she accepted her new labors and was soon one of the household.

FeverServe2.3.full: Each player **gains a SERVANT from LOST** and places it in their Quarters. *If you cannot gain a Servant, gain $1 instead.*

Dubious.2.full: Within days of their settling in to their spouse's liking, the local diocese sent a messenger to speak with each of the heirs about their father's charitability towards the diseased — or lack thereof. The bishop entreated them to donate precious time and money to help aid the sick at the church.
Dubious.2.easy: A few days after they had settled in the way their spouses liked, the local church sent a messenger to speak with each of the heirs about how much (or how little) their father had given to help the sick. The bishop asked them to give their valuable time and money to help the sick at the church.
Dubious.2.short: Days after they settled in, the bishop's messenger raised their father's lack of charity and urged the heirs to give time and money to the sick.

Dubious.3.full: Having an extensive background in biological studies at the university, the youths proudly offered their scientific services in subduing the epidemic. The bishop was unenthusiastic about the response and pressed them to change their mind — to no avail.
Dubious.3.easy: The young people had studied biology at university for a long time, so they proudly offered their scientific help to fight the epidemic. The bishop did not like this answer and tried to make them change their mind, but he failed.
Dubious.3.short: Proud biologists, they offered science against the epidemic instead. The bishop pressed them to reconsider, in vain.

Dubious.4.full: Retrieve the Dubious Bartering cards from the scenario box. Shuffle them and **give each player a Dubious Bartering card** and return any remaining to the box. This card is placed face-up near their Estate and is activated each time the listed action is taken.

ElecY.2.full: At the next town meeting, the townspeople were furious to discover a government official sent to survey a new extension to the electrical grid. The cousins' actions were noted in the minutes from that event where they disclosed their **support for the installation of electricity** and the proposed installation of it at zero cost to the town.
ElecY.2.easy: At the next town meeting, the townspeople were very angry to see a government official who had come to plan a new connection to the electricity network. The notes of the meeting recorded what the cousins had done: they said they gave their **support for the installation of electricity** and that it would cost the town nothing.
ElecY.2.short: At the next town meeting, a government surveyor for the electrical grid enraged the townspeople. The minutes recorded the cousins' **support for the installation of electricity**, at no cost to the town.

ElecY.3.full: In a mad display of various ignorances, an angry mob began to form in the center of town, forcing the scientists to retreat by carriage. The crowd soon burst into riotous fury, cursing the government and destroying everything in sight. The riot of 1912 is noted within town archives as the most violent in recorded history. The mob's flaming torches set the Hospital ablaze, leaving multiple individuals severely injured or deceased as they continued into the nearby hills.
ElecY.3.easy: Out of ignorance, an angry crowd came together in the town center, and the scientists had to escape in their carriage. The crowd soon went wild, cursed the government and destroyed everything they could see. The town records say that the riot of 1912 was the most violent one ever. The crowd's burning torches set the Hospital on fire, and many people were badly hurt or killed as the crowd moved on into the hills.
ElecY.3.short: An ignorant mob drove the scientists off by carriage, then rioted. The riot of 1912 was the town's most violent: torches set the Hospital ablaze, killing and maiming, as the mob moved into the hills.

ElecY.4.full: While the people's specific grievance had been long forgotten by the time the mob reached the steps of their estates, it was no less malicious in its issuance of flawed justice.
ElecY.4.easy: By the time the crowd reached the steps of their estates, everyone had long forgotten what exactly they were angry about. But their unfair kind of justice was just as cruel.
ElecY.4.short: By the time it reached their estates, the mob had forgotten its grievance, but not its malice.

ElecY.5.full: **Each player (regardless of their vote) must choose and discard an Estate Upgrade *(not a Storage Shed).***

ElecN.2.full: The townspeople sifted through the cousins' erudite proposal at the next town meeting and realized that they intended to **support their ridiculous distrust of modern convenience**. That evening, a celebratory mob congregated in town with various primitive lighting devices - given the lack of electricity - to cheer and chant their approval.
ElecN.2.easy: At the next town meeting, the townspeople read the cousins' clever proposal and understood that they wanted to **support their ridiculous distrust of modern convenience**. That evening, a happy crowd met in town with all kinds of old-fashioned lamps (there was no electricity, after all) to cheer and sing their approval.
ElecN.2.short: The townspeople realized the cousins would **support their ridiculous distrust of modern convenience**. That evening, a mob with primitive lamps gathered to cheer.

ElecN.3.full: Fueled by alcohol and inspired by ignorant revelry, the gathering quickly devolved into a riotous mass. Chanting loudly in crass language, they tore down the central streets of the village, leaving nothing untouched in their destructive path.
ElecN.3.easy: Full of alcohol and foolish joy, the party quickly turned into a riot. They shouted rude songs and ran wild through the main streets of the village, destroying everything in their way.
ElecN.3.short: Drunken revelry became a riot that tore through the village, destroying everything.

ElecN.4.full: In the morning, as the misty streets revealed themselves, the devastation and regret became clear as crystal. Newspapers of the time displayed pictures of the aftermath: the Hospital ablaze, the Town Hall left in smoldering ruins. They hastily rebuilt as best they could, but it would never be the same.
ElecN.4.easy: In the morning, when the fog cleared from the streets, the damage, and the people's regret, were very clear to see. The newspapers of that time showed pictures of what was left: the Hospital on fire, the Town Hall a smoking ruin. They quickly rebuilt as well as they could, but it would never be the same.
ElecN.4.short: Morning revealed the devastation: the Hospital ablaze, the Town Hall in ruins. They rebuilt in haste, but it would never be the same.

ElecN.5.full: Return the {icon:AngryMob_Icon} token to its starting location.

ElecN.6.full: The player that won the vote also receives **1 Ingredient or Knowledge** of their choice.

ElecN.7.full: Any player that voted **Yay** receives **1 Ingredient or Knowledge** of their choice.

Lettercode.2.full: As the welcome from the townspeople was considerably icy, the cousins were amused to receive a plain letter of correspondence sealed with wax. No return address was provided and no watermarks offered evidence as to their origin. Perhaps this mystery, they surmised, would afford them more than simple seclusion in this dreary countryside.
Lettercode.2.easy: The townspeople's welcome was very cold, so the cousins were amused to receive a simple letter closed with wax. There was no sender's address and no watermark to show where it came from. Maybe, they thought, this mystery would give them more than just a quiet life in this gloomy countryside.
Lettercode.2.short: Amid the townsfolk's icy welcome, the cousins received a wax-sealed letter with no return address. Perhaps it promised more than seclusion.

Lettercode.3.full: Little did they realize how instrumental this stealthful exchange would prove over the next several decades.
Lettercode.3.easy: They had no idea how important these secret letters would be over the next decades.
Lettercode.3.short: They had no idea how important it would prove.

NoUni3b.2.easy: Tired from old age and weak from a short return of Yellow Fever that was never cured, the scientists spend their last days weak and short of breath. Would this last important moment bring one great success that would prove their place in the history of science?
NoUni3b.2.short: Frail and wheezing after a return of the uncured Yellow Fever, would the scientists' final moment bring one triumph to secure their legacy?

Envelopes.3.easy: When I arrived at the place, I did my business as usual. As I was leaving, someone gently touched my shoulder. A woman in traditional clothes lifted her wool cap and asked me to follow her to a wooden bench nearby.
Envelopes.3.short: As I was leaving, a woman in traditional garb tapped my shoulder and led me to a nearby bench.

The town, no longer in complete poverty, began to attract new interest from those with both genuine and nefarious motivations. The true intent of the family members was revealed.
BuildingsEnd.2.easy: When they became old, the results of the family's investigations became known. The town was no longer completely poor, and it now attracted new people, some with honest and some with evil plans. The family members' true intentions were revealed.
BuildingsEnd.2.short: In their twilight years, their investigations bore fruit. The recovering town drew both honest and nefarious interest, and the family's true intent was revealed.

ProsperityHunterIntro.3.full: The disease had revealed a much deeper evil than the family could have ever expected: An evil ignorance that dwells within the minds of the people. It had not only left the previous generation in shambles, but imbued the townsfolk with a profound, insatiable fear, even as the town returned to relative stability. During the day, the people watched the forests, glimpsing dark shadows flitting between the trees. At night, they steeled themselves against the wailing howls of unseen terrors, dreading that their children would be stolen away from their beds.
ProsperityHunterIntro.3.easy: The disease had shown a much deeper evil than the family had ever expected: a dark ignorance in people's minds. It had destroyed the last generation, and it had filled the townspeople with a deep fear that never ended, even when life in town became more normal again. During the day, people watched the forests and saw dark shadows moving quickly between the trees. At night, they listened in fear to the howls of creatures they could not see, afraid that their children would be taken from their beds.
ProsperityHunterIntro.3.short: The disease had revealed a deeper evil: ignorance. Even as the town recovered, fear ruled. By day, shadows flitted between the trees; by night, unseen things howled, and parents feared for their children.

ProsperityHunterIntro.4.full: That was until the Fraternity of Hunters, emboldened by the success of their clandestine operations, emerged from the shadows on the night of a blood red moon. They wore long-tail coats of black, burgundy, and dark leather, a wooden cross hanging either from their necks or dangling from their sides. They clutched crossbows, whips, and daggers freshly glimmering with crimson fluid. Their blood-stained attire and steel-eyed gaze evoked the undaunted presence of ones who had peered into the void and returned forever changed.
ProsperityHunterIntro.4.easy: That changed when the Fraternity of Hunters, made bold by the success of their secret work, came out of the shadows on the night of a blood-red moon. They wore long coats of black, dark red and dark leather, with a wooden cross around their necks or at their sides. They held crossbows, whips and daggers that were still shining with fresh red blood. Their bloody clothes and hard eyes showed people who had looked into the darkness and come back changed forever.
ProsperityHunterIntro.4.short: Then, under a blood red moon, the Fraternity of Hunters emerged: long dark coats, wooden crosses, crossbows, whips and bloodied daggers. Their eyes had looked into the void.

ProsperityHunterIntro.5.full: Their stated goal: to slay every last beast in the land and return those who had unleashed this foul plague back to the depths of hell from whence they came. The Fraternity turned the fear of the populace to their advantage. They fed the superstitions of the people, blaming the sickness and disease on fiendish creatures from the dark.
ProsperityHunterIntro.5.easy: They said their goal was to kill every last beast in the land, and to send those who had started this terrible plague back to hell, where they came from. The Fraternity used the people's fear for its own purposes. They made the people's superstitions stronger and blamed the sickness and disease on evil creatures from the darkness.
ProsperityHunterIntro.5.short: They vowed to slay every beast and send those who unleashed the plague back to hell. Feeding the people's superstitions, they blamed the disease on fiends from the dark.

ProsperityHunterIntro.6.full: While they did not require monetary compensation in return, what they did ask was much more severe. Their sanguine efforts could not be completed in isolation, so on nights when the blood moon rose high in the evening sky, a handful of townsfolk were chosen to assist the Hunters' party and venture into the unknown. The next morning, the surviving Hunters would return, their garments speckled in the blood of the beasts and holding aloft the severed trophies of monsters slain in the wilderness. It was only a matter of time before they would call upon the family.
ProsperityHunterIntro.6.easy: They did not want money in return, but what they asked for was much worse. They could not do their bloody work alone. So on nights when the blood moon rose high in the sky, a few townspeople were chosen to go with the Hunters into the unknown. The next morning, the Hunters who survived came back, their clothes covered in drops of the beasts' blood, holding up the cut-off body parts of the monsters they had killed in the wild. Sooner or later, they would come to the family.
ProsperityHunterIntro.6.short: They wanted no money, but something worse: on blood moon nights, townsfolk were chosen to join their hunts. The survivors returned at dawn with bloody trophies. Soon they would call upon the family.

ProsperityHunterIntro.7.full: Perhaps driven by a sense of limited time or jealousy over the Hunters' ability to frighten the townsfolk even moreso than their own actions, the cousins continued their meticulous labors in earnest. However, they were deeply unaware of just how intertwined their fates would be to the Fraternity.
ProsperityHunterIntro.7.easy: Maybe because they felt time was running out, or because they were jealous that the Hunters could frighten the townspeople even more than they could, the cousins went on with their careful work with new energy. But they had no idea how closely their future would be connected to the Fraternity.
ProsperityHunterIntro.7.short: Pressed for time, or jealous of the Hunters' power to frighten, the cousins worked on, unaware how bound their fates were to the Fraternity.

DiseaseConsequence.2.full: While their parents may have escaped the harshness of the Yellow Fever epidemic thanks to their aristocratic distance from the populace, the young scientists were unable to avoid the effects of such dismal environs. As the years passed, they found themselves stricken with a chronic illness that would remain with them for their entire lives. The enfeeblement haunted their work, insomuch that many weeks at a time were spent in isolation and bed rest.
DiseaseConsequence.2.easy: Their parents may have escaped the worst of the Yellow Fever epidemic, because as aristocrats they lived far from the common people. But the young scientists could not escape the effects of such a terrible place. Over the years, they caught a long-lasting illness that stayed with them all their lives. This weakness made their work hard, and they often had to stay alone in bed for many weeks.
DiseaseConsequence.2.short: Unlike their aloof parents, the young scientists could not escape the fever. A chronic illness struck them for life, often confining them to bed for weeks.

DiseaseConsequence.3.full: In their individual ways, the group set to work on something to alleviate or cure these symptoms, knowing that if they were unsuccessful, **the disease would carry over to their progeny.**
DiseaseConsequence.3.easy: Each in their own way, they started working on something to make these symptoms better or to cure them. They knew that if they failed, **the disease would carry over to their progeny.** (their children)

DiseaseConsequence.4.full: Retrieve the Hereditary Disease cards from the Scenario box. Shuffle them and **deal one Disease card face-up** to each player near their Masterwork. Return the remaining Hereditary Disease cards to the box.

HospitalDefine.3.full: Look through the Experiment deck of your choice to find an Experiment of your choice and draw it into your hand. *(Once complete, shuffle the deck.)*

HospitalDefine.4.full: You have until the beginning of your next turn to complete this action *(allow other players to begin their turn while you choose).*

HospitalDefine.5.full: NOTE: You may take the Hospital action with any legal token, but you must only click on the Storybook prompt the **first time** you visit the Hospital with your Self.

DevastationIntro.3.full: Following a bitter winter in 1862, a second epidemic descended upon the village in all its visceral and bloody force. This time, however, the town was unable to recover. Buildings were left to rot as the sick fled into the countryside. Some escaped to shelter in camps near Bucharest, while the less fortunate collapsed on the icy pathways along the journey, their frozen flesh left to thaw along muddy roadsides with the change of seasons. Lost and hopeless without aid, the town dwindled until only the barest of amenities remained.
DevastationIntro.3.easy: After a hard winter in 1862, a second epidemic came to the village with all its bloody force. But this time, the town could not recover. Buildings were left to rot as the sick escaped into the countryside. Some found safety in camps near Bucharest. Others were less lucky and fell down on the icy paths along the way; their frozen bodies were left by the muddy roads to thaw when the seasons changed. Without help, the town lost hope and shrank until only the most basic things were left.
DevastationIntro.3.short: After the bitter winter of 1862, a second epidemic struck, and the town did not recover. The sick fled; some reached camps near Bucharest, others froze on the roads. The town dwindled to almost nothing.

DevastationIntro.4.full: The desolation to which the family returned was unlike anything they had experienced in their short lifetime and the joys of youthful marriage were swiftly eclipsed by the reality of disease. Those who had stubbornly refused to join the others in mass exodus burned incense in their homes to prevent miasmatic transference of the fever; a practice quickly adopted within the family's estates. For years, the ominous tintinnabulation echoed across the stricken valley each night to ward off the disease even as the cemetery was inundated with new bodies.
DevastationIntro.4.easy: The family came back to a ruin that was worse than anything they had seen in their short lives, and the happiness of being young and newly married quickly disappeared because of the disease. The people who had refused to leave with the others burned incense in their homes to stop the bad air from spreading the fever, and the family soon did the same in their estates. For years, bells rang every night across the sick valley to keep the disease away, while the cemetery filled with new bodies.
DevastationIntro.4.short: The desolation eclipsed the joys of young marriage. Those who stayed burned incense against the miasma, as did the family, and for years bells tolled each night while the cemetery filled.

DevastationIntro.5.full: For most, this environment of sullen quiet and isolation would cause one to question their sanity, but for the scientists, this time was marked by a signature productivity. Perhaps the thought of redemption drove them forward or the constant reminder of their own mortality with each passing moment. Either way, they each toiled away in their studies, confident that through tragedy their family's legacy would finally be secured forever in the annals of science!
DevastationIntro.5.easy: For most people, so much sad silence and loneliness would make them doubt if they were still sane. But for the scientists, this was a time of great productivity. Maybe they wanted to make up for the past, or maybe every moment reminded them that they too would die. Either way, they all worked hard at their studies, sure that through this tragedy their family's name would finally have its place in the history of science forever!
DevastationIntro.5.short: Where others might have gone mad, the scientists thrived. Driven by redemption or mortality, they toiled on, sure that tragedy would secure their legacy forever!

DevastationIntro.6.full: And the country began to take notice of their activities; though not in the academic manner which they anticipated. Shadowy figures kept their watchful eye on the region with mysterious intentions. Unaware of the sinister machinations afoot, the scientists blindly immersed themselves in their work. They would soon find themselves confronted by a choice that would rock the very foundations of scientific (and rational) thought as they understood it.
DevastationIntro.6.easy: And the country began to notice what they were doing, but not in the academic way they had hoped for. Mysterious people secretly watched the region, with unknown plans. The scientists did not see these dark plans and only thought about their work. Soon they would have to make a choice that would shake the base of scientific (and logical) thinking as they knew it.
DevastationIntro.6.short: The country took notice, though not as they hoped. Shadowy figures watched the region while the scientists worked on, blind to it. A choice would soon shake the foundations of science and reason.

Immortality.2.full: If not now, then when? The cousins pored over this question. How long would they remain relegated to an eccentric footnote murmured amongst the townspeople? Why must they toil in their most important labors under the cover of darkness and stone like vermin? A deep restlessness had set into the minds of each, and even on the cusp of approval from the academic community, they could not quell these thoughts.
Immortality.2.easy: If not now, when? The cousins thought about this question for a long time. How long would they stay a strange little story that the townspeople whispered about? Why did they have to do their most important work hidden in darkness and behind stone walls, like rats? They all felt very restless, and even now, when the academic world was almost ready to accept them, they could not stop these thoughts.
Immortality.2.short: If not now, when? How long would they remain a whispered footnote, working in darkness like vermin? Even near academic approval, their restlessness grew.

Immortality.3.full: It was trivial to discuss meager experimentations when the solidification of such a poignant legacy repeated fruitlessly generation upon generation. If only time was no longer an obstacle.
Immortality.3.easy: Small experiments were not important when building a great legacy failed again and again, generation after generation. If only time was not a problem anymore.
Immortality.3.short: Small experiments seemed trivial while their legacy failed generation after generation. If only time were no obstacle.

Immortality.4.full: They vowed to accumulate a wealth of knowledge in their fields of expertise that far surpassed the pitiable ruminations of ancient scholars. Perhaps if they pushed forward into the unknown they would harness new and untold powers. Their evening conversations spurred them to devise a way to cheat the most sacred and inevitable truth of existence.
Immortality.4.easy: They promised to collect much more knowledge in their fields than the poor ideas of ancient scholars. Maybe if they went further into the unknown, they would find new and unknown powers. Their evening talks made them look for a way to cheat the most holy and certain truth of life.
Immortality.4.short: They vowed to surpass the ancient scholars and harness untold powers. Their evening talks turned to cheating life's most inevitable truth.

Immortality.5.full: For if life can be taken and altered by humanity into its most cruel and twisted form, surely that same spark could be endlessly preserved!
Immortality.5.easy: Because if people can take life and change it into its most cruel and twisted form, then surely they can also keep that same spark alive forever!
Immortality.5.short: If life could be twisted into its cruelest form, surely its spark could be preserved forever!

Immortality.7.full: Each player chooses an incomplete track of their choice in their Journal and places their {icon:Storybook} token on the third level of that track.

DetEffect1.2.full: It could not continue. Sick and unable to heal again, stumbling blindly until the bones were brittle enough to snap, their bodies had finally failed them. And when the mind had joined the fragile physical form in its inability to perform the most basic of functions, the struggle ceased.
DetEffect1.2.easy: It could not go on. They were sick and could not heal again. They stumbled around blindly until their bones were so weak that they broke. Their bodies had finally given up. And when the mind, like the weak body, could no longer do even the simplest things, the fight was over.
DetEffect1.2.short: It could not continue. Sick, unhealing, their bones brittle, their bodies failed, then their minds, and the struggle ceased.

DetEffect1.3.full: Death in all its inevitability had finally claimed them.
DetEffect1.3.easy: In the end, death, which nobody can escape, had taken them.

DetEffect1.4.full: Unfortunately, their body was in such an advanced state of degradation it could not even be used for further experimentation. This made the grief more substantial.
DetEffect1.4.easy: Sadly, their body was in such a bad condition that it could not even be used for more experiments. This made the sadness even greater.
DetEffect1.4.short: Sadly, their body was too decayed even for experiments, which deepened the grief.

DetEffect1.5.full: Any player with an **Immortality card** discards a **Caretaker** to Lost.

DetEffect1.6.full: Discard all **Immortality cards** to the scenario box.

DetEffect2.2.full: They feared that their hasty solution had borne upon them irreversible effects. The interior withered, the skin grayed and sagged translucently against the sinewy veins beneath. The ultimate cure had become a curse and life was like a festering wound that cut deeper with each passing day. Still, they continued on in their work, hoping the effects were temporary but fearing the worst. It took more and more resources to quell their pain each day.
DetEffect2.2.easy: They were afraid that their quick solution had caused damage that could not be undone. Their body dried up inside; their skin turned gray and hung loose and thin over the veins underneath. The perfect cure had become a curse, and life was like an infected wound that went deeper every day. Still they went on with their work, hoping the effects would pass, but fearing the worst. Every day they needed more and more to stop the pain.
DetEffect2.2.short: Their hasty cure had become a curse: withered, gray, translucent skin over sinewy veins, life a festering wound. They worked on, hoping it would pass, needing ever more to dull the pain.

DetEffect2.3.full: Any player with an **Immortality card** discards an **Ingredient** *if possible* and **draws a Compulsion**.

DetEffect3.2.full: All and all, the continued effects of their approach to Immortality had fared exceptionally well. While the skin displayed liver spots and an amount of vigor had been lost as the blood cooled with age, the effects were only a distraction. At most, a gangrenous finger had to be excised once every few years, but what was one extraneous extremity compared to the ability to assist in the most important scientific discoveries the world had ever known?
DetEffect3.2.easy: All in all, their way to Immortality had worked very well over time. Their skin had age spots, and they had lost some energy as their blood became colder with age, but these were only small problems. At most, a rotting finger had to be cut off once every few years. But what is one finger more or less, if you can help with the most important scientific discoveries the world has ever known?
DetEffect3.2.short: Their Immortality had fared exceptionally well. Liver spots and cooling blood were mere distractions; what was the odd gangrenous finger, excised every few years, against the greatest discoveries the world had known?

DetEffect3.3.full: Any player with an **Immortality card** loses **{0}VP**.

DetEffect4.2.full: The unthinkable had been achieved. Whether by sheer providence or remarkable display of intellect, the solution to immortality appeared to have worked! In fact, the effects were so remarkable that many witness accounts of the day observed that the aging process appeared to have reversed. While still aged by all accounts, their individual treatise on Immortality appeared to have succeeded.
DetEffect4.2.easy: They had done the impossible. Whether by pure luck or by great intelligence, their way to immortality seemed to work! The effects were so amazing that many people at the time said that they seemed to be getting younger. They were still old, everyone agreed, but each of their works on Immortality seemed to be a success.
DetEffect4.2.short: The unthinkable had been achieved: immortality worked! Witnesses even claimed their aging had reversed.

InfinityClick2.3.easy: There is no doubt in my {0}. Now that this research is finished, {1} Time will no longer harm my work, and I will be free to face the {2} without the limits of a mortal body!
InfinityClick2.3.short: There is no doubt in my {0}. With this research complete, {1} Time will no longer hinder me, and I will face the {2} unimpeded by this mortal coil!

InfinityClick1.2.full: It seemed unimaginable; not simply a cure for all disease, but a mysterious contrivance to extend life indefinitely. Perhaps, those that pursued this heretical course of action should not have postulated, "could it be done?" Instead, they might have asked themselves, "but at what cost?"
InfinityClick1.2.easy: It seemed impossible: not just a cure for every disease, but a mysterious way to make life last forever. Maybe the people who followed this forbidden path should not have asked "Can it be done?" Maybe they should have asked: "But what will it cost?"
InfinityClick1.2.short: Not just a cure for all disease, but endless life. Perhaps they should have asked not "could it be done?" but "at what cost?"

UniImmortal.2.short: Inheriting from a living parent unnerved the heirs and their unknowing spouses, but the surprisingly spry parent proved useful help on the Estate.

UniImmortal.3.short: Those whose parents had chosen a gentler fate had nothing to hide, and drew less suspicion.

DevEventCure.6.easy: "The brotherhood has heard about your suffering, and we want to offer you a trade. For a little knowledge, we give you a cure. Drink this liquid and your terrible illness will end," she said, as lightning flashed across the sky.
DevEventCure.6.short: "The brotherhood offers a trade: a little knowledge for a cure. Drink, and your affliction will cease," she said, as lightning split the sky.

HubertusWolves2.1.full: **Carefully pick up the storybook and do not allow any other players to see the screen.**

HubertusWolves2.3.full: I, {0}, am writing this letter to you after my meeting with an associate of the International Order of St. Hubertus. Our conversation was brief, but the resulting knowledge has piqued my curiosities.
HubertusWolves2.3.easy: I, {0}, am writing to you after I met a member of the International Order of St. Hubertus. We did not talk for long, but what I learned has made me very curious.
HubertusWolves2.3.short: I, {0}, write after a brief meeting with a member of the International Order of St. Hubertus that piqued my curiosity.

HubertusWolves2.4.full: It has been revealed to me that your intentions are

HubertusWolves2.5.full: nefarious. The malevolent Order is consumed with greed, seeking to unearth the ancient secrets in this area and use this power to alter humanity and spread a plague of monstrous entities across the world. You only asked for your work to remain **concealed**.
HubertusWolves2.5.easy: evil. The wicked Order is full of greed. It wants to dig up the old secrets of this area and use their power to change humanity and spread a plague of monsters across the world. You only asked me to keep your work **concealed**.
HubertusWolves2.5.short: nefarious. The greedy Order seeks this area's ancient secrets, to alter humanity and spread monsters across the world. You only asked for your work to stay **concealed**.

HubertusWolves2.6.full: demonstrably positive. The Order is only concerned with establishing a safe haven for those afflicted by disease. Your representative even revealed a physical peculiarity that had elongated her cuspids into sharp points. She left swiftly before nightfall, ignoring my pleas for her to remain, but she urged me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to become apparent.
HubertusWolves2.6.easy: clearly good. The Order only wants to build a safe place for people who suffer from disease. Your messenger even showed me something strange about her body: her canine teeth had grown into sharp points. She left quickly before dark, even though I begged her to stay, but she told me to **investigate** the secret work that would soon come to light.
HubertusWolves2.6.short: demonstrably positive. The Order seeks only a safe haven for the diseased. Your envoy, her canines grown into sharp points, left before nightfall, urging me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to surface.

HubertusWolves2.7.full: Being intimately familiar with matters of the occult, this admission is unsurprising. My apprehensions are only related to how your actions will impact my ability to advance my scientific studies most generously.
HubertusWolves2.7.easy: I know the world of the occult very well, so this news does not surprise me. I am only worried about how your actions will affect my own scientific work.
HubertusWolves2.7.short: Versed in the occult, I am unsurprised. I only worry how your actions will affect my research.

Diseases1.2.full: Even the most agile mind cannot willingly escape the frailness of the human form. As such, the foul plague upon the household syphoned a considerable energy from their work and left them bed-ridden for months on end.
Diseases1.2.easy: Even the quickest mind cannot escape the weakness of the human body. The terrible plague in the house took a lot of energy away from their work, and they had to stay in bed for months.
Diseases1.2.short: No mind escapes the body's frailty. The plague left them bed-ridden for months.

Diseases1.4.full: It seemed that the cousins were fortunate in their early years. Even the most agile mind cannot willingly escape the frailness of the human form. However, with a strict regimen of rest, diet, and bloodletting, these deficiencies could mostly be nullified.
Diseases1.4.easy: It seemed that the cousins were lucky when they were young. Even the quickest mind cannot escape the weakness of the human body. But with strict rules for rest and food, and with bloodletting, they could mostly stop these weaknesses.
Diseases1.4.short: The cousins were fortunate early on. With rest, diet and bloodletting, their frailties were mostly kept at bay.

Diseases1.5.full: All players that have not completed the **Hereditary Disease Experiment** must **discard a Knowledge cube to the supply** or **lose 2VP**.

Diseases1.6.full: The Hereditary disease has no effect.

HubertusHunters1.1.full: **Carefully pick up the storybook and do not allow any other players to see the screen.**

HubertusHunters1.3.full: I, {0}, am writing this letter to you after my meeting with an associate of the International Fraternity of Hunters. Our secret conversation over brunch was quite revealing, and the resulting knowledge has piqued my interests.
HubertusHunters1.3.easy: I, {0}, am writing to you after I met a member of the International Fraternity of Hunters. Our secret conversation over brunch told me a lot, and what I learned has made me very interested.
HubertusHunters1.3.short: I, {0}, write after a secret brunch with a member of the International Fraternity of Hunters that piqued my interest.

HubertusHunters1.4.full: It has been revealed to me that your intentions are

HubertusHunters1.5.full: amusingly exploitative. The Fraternity hopes to use the recent epidemic as a cover for their activities to unearth ancient supernatural secrets in the region and use them for monetary and political gain. Although I remain skeptical, if these labors are successful, I will be deeply interested in the results. You only asked for your work to remain **concealed**.
HubertusHunters1.5.easy: selfish in a funny way. The Fraternity wants to use the recent epidemic to hide what it is really doing: digging up old supernatural secrets in the region and using them to gain money and political power. I still have my doubts, but if this work succeeds, I will be very interested in the results. You only asked me to keep your work **concealed**.
HubertusHunters1.5.short: amusingly exploitative. The Fraternity uses the epidemic as cover to unearth supernatural secrets for money and power. If it works, I will be interested. You only asked for your work to stay **concealed**.

HubertusHunters1.6.full: good. It was astute for you to note how oddly silent the town has remained over the last few years. Keeping a watchful eye over the proceedings, the Fraternity appears only concerned with rooting out who or what is behind this veil of secrecy. You've urged me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to become apparent.
HubertusHunters1.6.easy: good. You were right to notice how strangely quiet the town has been in the last few years. The Fraternity is watching what happens, and it only seems to want to find out who or what is hiding behind all this secrecy. You asked me to **investigate** the secret work that will soon come to light.
HubertusHunters1.6.short: good. You noted how strangely silent the town has been. The Fraternity only seeks what hides behind the secrecy. You urged me to **investigate** the secret workings soon to surface.

HubertusHunters1.7.full: Being an entrepreneur myself, in a fashion, these goals are not so misaligned with my own. My apprehensions are only related to how your actions will impact my ability to advance my scientific studies most generously.
HubertusHunters1.7.easy: I am a businessperson myself, in a way, so these goals are not so different from mine. I am only worried about how your actions will affect my own scientific work.
HubertusHunters1.7.short: As an entrepreneur of sorts, I find these goals close to mine. I only worry how your actions will affect my research.

DevastationFate1.2.full: Remove all player pieces from the board and Perform the End of a Generation. Return any remaining {icon:StorybookToken} tokens to the supply.

DevastationFate1.3.full: The ties that bound the family to these secret warring factions changed the course of history.
DevastationFate1.3.easy: The family's ties to these secret groups at war with each other changed the course of history.
DevastationFate1.3.short: The family's ties to these secret factions changed history.

DevastationFate1.4.full: While secrets could not forever be kept, the silent assistance of {0} influential members of the upper crust ensured that the **Hunters** could progress in their endeavors long enough to make their presence integral to the town. For a price, they swore to protect all citizens from the disease and darkness that had enveloped the countryside.
DevastationFate1.4.easy: Secrets could not be kept forever. But {0} powerful members of high society secretly helped the **Hunters**, so the Hunters could continue their work long enough to become an important part of the town. For a price, they promised to protect all citizens from the disease and the darkness that had covered the countryside.
DevastationFate1.4.short: With the silent help of {0} influential aristocrats, the **Hunters** became integral to the town. For a price, they swore to protect all from disease and darkness.

DevastationFate1.5.easy: Because the evil work of the **Order of St. Hubertus,** was exposed, it got too much attention and had to leave the region. DevastationFate1.5.short: Exposed, the **Order of St. Hubertus,** had to leave. The **Fraternity of Hunters** built a stronghold in town, sworn to protect it from all evil.

DevastationFate1.6.easy: Secrets could not be kept forever. But {0} powerful members of high society secretly helped the **Order**, so the Order could continue its work long enough to become an important part of the town. They started to carry out their plans at once.
DevastationFate1.6.short: With the silent help of {0} influential aristocrats, the **Order** became integral to the town, and at once advanced its schemes.

DevastationFate1.7.full: By exposing the insidious deeds of the **Fraternity of Hunters,** the additional attention forced them to quit the region. Motivated by the promise of swift justice, the **Order of St. Hubertus** created a stronghold in the town. They swore to provide a haven for all outcasts.
DevastationFate1.7.easy: Because the evil actions of the **Fraternity of Hunters,** were exposed, it got too much attention and had to leave the region. BuildingSignin.2.easy: After their visit, the strange behavior of the workers and the perfectly clean furniture made them even more curious. A few days later, they decided to leave their scientific work for one evening and investigate the {0}.

BuildingSignin.3.full: **Please choose which player is making this investigation:**

BuildplayA.1.full: **Do not allow the other players to see the Storybook while making the decision below.**

BuildplayA.3.full: I arrived at the {0} under cover of darkness. I was ill-suited for such stealthy missions, but I kept my cloak and collar about my neck to conceal my identity in case I was discovered.
BuildplayA.3.easy: I arrived at the {0} when it was dark. I am not good at secret missions like this, but I kept my cloak and collar up around my neck, so that nobody would know me if they found me.
BuildplayA.3.short: I arrived at the {0} after dark, cloak and collar raised to hide my identity.

BuildplayA.4.full: A thick fog shrouded my approach on the cool night that I chose to investigate the {0}. I asked the carriage driver to await my return on the outskirts of town, while I stole away into the empty streets. Nary a soul was about on this evening, and I was soon inside without arousing suspicion.
BuildplayA.4.easy: On the cool night I chose to investigate the {0}, thick fog hid me as I came closer. I asked the driver to wait for me at the edge of town and quietly went into the empty streets. Nobody was outside that evening, and soon I was inside without anyone getting suspicious.
BuildplayA.4.short: Fog hid my approach to the {0}. Leaving my carriage at the edge of town, I slipped through the empty streets and inside unnoticed.

BuildplayA.5.full: To my chagrin, a {0} stood near the front door of the building. At this late hour, I could only assume that they were standing guard. Not to be thwarted so easily, I tilted my hat to obscure my face and stalked into the alley behind. The lock on the rear door was a trifle for my tools, and I entered without a sound.
BuildplayA.5.easy: To my annoyance, a {0} was standing near the front door of the building. So late at night, I could only think that they were keeping guard. I did not give up so easily: I pulled my hat down over my face and quietly went into the alley behind the building. The lock on the back door was easy for my tools, and I went in without a sound.
BuildplayA.5.short: A {0} stood guard at the front door. Hat low, I slipped into the alley behind, picked the rear lock and entered silently.

Trigger35Points.1.full: **Carefully hand this storybook device to the player that just reached 35VP. This is read within view of all players.**

Trigger35Points.3.full: To reach the pinnacle of understanding, only to feel the cruel hand of treachery. The rest of the family was noticeably not distraught when a recent article in the regional newspaper spread an uncomfortable rumor about my personal hygiene.
Trigger35Points.3.easy: I reached the highest level of understanding, only to feel the cruel hand of betrayal. The rest of the family was clearly not upset when an article in the regional newspaper spread an embarrassing rumor about how clean I am.
Trigger35Points.3.short: At the pinnacle of understanding, I was betrayed: my family seemed unbothered by a newspaper rumor about my hygiene.

Trigger35Points.4.full: I do not have time for this interruption! I do not smell like pickles! It is the formaldehyde solution for my most recent experiment. It is not the smell of pickles; it is the smell of SCIENCE!
Trigger35Points.4.easy: I have no time for this disturbance! I do not smell like pickles! It is the formaldehyde liquid for my latest experiment. It is not the smell of pickles; it is the smell of SCIENCE!
Trigger35Points.4.short: I do not smell like pickles! It is formaldehyde. It is the smell of SCIENCE!

Trigger35Points.7.full: I awoke this evening to find my home on fire and the culprits nowhere to be found. But, I know who did it. I could still smell the chemical reaction as the fires raged. I would have never expected my cousins to stoop to such a base level. Direct and blatant sabotage? Absolutely unconscionable.
Trigger35Points.7.easy: This evening I woke up and found my house on fire, and the people who did it were gone. But I know who it was. I could still smell the chemical reaction while the fire burned. I never thought my cousins would go so low. Open, deliberate sabotage? Completely unacceptable.
Trigger35Points.7.short: I awoke to my house ablaze. I could smell the chemicals; I know it was my cousins. Blatant sabotage? Unconscionable.

Trigger35Points.8.full: It will take weeks for my spouse to manage the removal of the damaged piece of our Estate. They are all just jealous of my genius!

Trigger35Points.10.full: Immediately **lose 4VP** and **discard an Estate Upgrade of your choice**.

ChooseScience.4.full: It has been three days since I received a letter from the Hungarian government and two days since my cousins deigned it necessary to make me the target of their ridicule. My parents cared deeply for this horrid community - a sentiment that those miscreants know nothing about!
ChooseScience.4.easy: Three days ago I got a letter from the Hungarian government, and two days ago my cousins decided to make fun of me. My parents cared very much about this terrible town, a feeling those troublemakers know nothing about!
ChooseScience.4.short: Three days since the government's letter, two since my cousins began mocking me. My parents cared for this horrid town, which those miscreants cannot understand!

ChooseScience.5.full: I am not some groveler who needs confirmation from the stuffed shirts and upturned noses of European academies. But, getting to choose the **subject of the upcoming Symposium** that could very well determine if a **University** is built in {0}?

ChooseScience.5.short: I need no approval from Europe's academies. But choosing the **subject of the upcoming Symposium**, which may decide whether a **University** is built in {0}?

ChooseScience.6.full: My parents instilled into me a scientific vigor that far surpasses even the members of my own, somewhat beloved, family. As I returned from studies abroad, it was my own aptitudes that spearheaded my cousins into action. Damn them and their jibes! I will show them. In fact, I have already made my choice and penned my response. It will be I who will be doing the laughing in the end.
ChooseScience.6.easy: My parents gave me a passion for science that is much stronger than that of the rest of my (somewhat loved) family. When I came back from studying abroad, it was my talent that got my cousins moving. Damn them and their jokes! I will show them. In fact, I have already made my choice and written my answer. In the end, I will be the one laughing.
ChooseScience.6.short: My scientific vigor surpasses my family's; it was I who spurred my cousins into action. Damn their jibes! I have made my choice, and I will laugh last.

SymposiumEvent1.2.full: The journey to the newly created city of Budapest for the {0} Symposium was uncharacteristically dour. However, this dreadful murkiness could not dampen the spirits of the {1}; nor could the sojourn in the marginal accommodations prepared for their arrival. For the cousins, this recognition for their efforts to advance science at all costs was considerably well-deserved and long-overdue.
SymposiumEvent1.2.easy: The trip to the new city of Budapest for the {0} Symposium was unusually gloomy. But the bad weather could not spoil the good mood of the {1}, and neither could the poor rooms that had been prepared for them. For the cousins, this recognition of their work to push science forward, whatever the cost, was well deserved and had come far too late.
SymposiumEvent1.2.short: The trip to Budapest for the {0} Symposium was dreary, but nothing could dampen the {1}'s spirits. Recognition was long overdue.

SymposiumEvent1.3.full: The University was abuzz with activity as they attended various events and offered their prescribed greetings.
SymposiumEvent1.3.easy: The University was very busy as they went to different events and said the expected hellos.
SymposiumEvent1.3.short: The University buzzed as they made their rounds.

SanityChoice.2.full: **{0}. This choice is read and made within view of all players.**

SanityChoice.4.full: The fools! The utter fools! In their haste to return to their amateurish attempts at science, my dear, witless cousins have been overlooked by our colleagues at the university. And so it fell to me to advise them on this most important psychological matter!
SanityChoice.4.easy: Fools! Complete fools! My dear, stupid cousins were in such a hurry to get back to their amateur science that our colleagues at the university have ignored them. So it is my job to advise them on this very important question of the mind!
SanityChoice.4.short: Fools! Rushing back to their amateur science, my witless cousins were passed over by the university. So it falls to me to decide this psychological matter!

SanityChoice.5.full: My in-depth studies of phrenology and first-hand observation of brain function have allowed me to calculate with flawless accuracy the appropriate level of mental intensity needed to excel in science; the most proper balance of passion and ethical ambiguity.
SanityChoice.5.easy: My deep studies of phrenology (the shape of the skull) and my own observations of how the brain works have let me calculate, without any mistake, how much mental intensity you need to be great at science: the best balance of passion and flexible morals.
SanityChoice.5.short: Phrenology and observation let me calculate exactly the mental intensity science requires: the proper balance of passion and ethical ambiguity.

SanityChoice.6.full: While, yes, we may ALL benefit from this assessment and yes, they did only consult me out of a sense of pity, it is I alone that will now control the fate of us all!
SanityChoice.6.easy: Yes, we may ALL profit from this assessment, and yes, they only asked me because they felt sorry for me. But now I alone will control what happens to all of us!
SanityChoice.6.short: Yes, we ALL benefit, and yes, they asked me out of pity. But I alone now control our fate!

HospitalVisitCheck.2.easy: The {0} General Hospital was one of the first hospitals in the region. It opened in 1865, and it helped to change what people thought about hospitals: not a place where you go to die, but a place where you get well, with the most modern medicine.
HospitalVisitCheck.2.short: Founded in 1865, the {0} General Hospital, among the region's first, made hospitals places of healing instead of dying.

HospitalVisitCheck2.2.full: **Visitation Report: Dr. {0} - Notes submitted by Nurse Varga**

HospitalVisitCheck2.3.full: Dr. {0} seemed in a hurry. Dismissed each area as sterile and uninspired. Until we arrived at the operating room. Immediately became enraptured, fixated, and I had to thrice repeat myself before they responded.
HospitalVisitCheck2.3.easy: Dr. {0} seemed to be in a hurry. Said every area was too clean and boring. Until we got to the operating room. Was suddenly fascinated, could not look away, and I had to say everything three times before they answered.
HospitalVisitCheck2.3.short: Dr. {0} hurried through, dismissing everything, until the operating room. Then they were transfixed and did not hear me.

HospitalVisitCheck2.4.full: "This is all wrong. What do they teach in these surgeon schools?" Dr. {0} asked, clearly not expecting an answer and brazenly entered the operating room to accost the surgeons on duty. They retrieved a scalpel and insisting on completing the operation themselves. I have never seen so much blood.
HospitalVisitCheck2.4.easy: "This is all wrong. What do they teach at these surgeon schools?" asked Dr. {0}, clearly not expecting an answer, and boldly walked into the operating room to confront the surgeons on duty. They took a scalpel and insisted on finishing the operation themselves. I have never seen so much blood.
HospitalVisitCheck2.4.short: "This is all wrong. What do they teach in these surgeon schools?" Dr. {0} stormed in, seized a scalpel and finished the operation. I have never seen so much blood.

HospitalVisitCheck2.5.full: Their response was muffled and I was unable to stop them from entering the theater. Their face was etched in a hideous grin as they stood at the center with their hands raised into the air. At this point, they either refused to listen or entered a catatonic state which left them motionless for nearly an hour.
HospitalVisitCheck2.5.easy: I could not understand their answer, and I could not stop them from going into the operating room. They stood in the middle with their hands up in the air and a horrible grin on their face. Then they either refused to listen or fell into a kind of trance, and they did not move for almost an hour.
HospitalVisitCheck2.5.short: I could not stop them entering the theater. They stood at its center, arms raised, grinning hideously, then went motionless for nearly an hour.

HospitalVisitCheck2.6.full: At this point, {0} had to be escorted by security from the premises. They are barred from any further tours of the facilities.
HospitalVisitCheck2.6.easy: At this point, security had to take {0} out of the building. They are not allowed on any more tours of the hospital.
HospitalVisitCheck2.6.short: Security removed {0}. They are barred from further tours.

HospitalVisitCheck2.8.full: Relatively uneventful visit, though unsettling. Dr. {0} requested a tour through the wards.
HospitalVisitCheck2.8.easy: A fairly quiet visit, but a disturbing one. Dr. {0} asked for a tour of the wards.
HospitalVisitCheck2.8.short: Uneventful but unsettling. Dr. {0} toured the wards.

HospitalVisitCheck2.9.full: Mostly disinterested and silent. However, our visit to the morgue was longer than to my liking. Dr. {0} kept insisting on inspecting the more extreme cases, excitedly asking questions while I unsuccessfully attempted to stop them from physically handling the deceased.
HospitalVisitCheck2.9.easy: Mostly bored and silent. But our visit to the morgue was longer than I liked. Dr. {0} kept asking to look at the worst cases and asked excited questions, while I tried, and failed, to stop them from touching the dead bodies.
HospitalVisitCheck2.9.short: Silent, until the morgue. Dr. {0} lingered over the worst cases and kept handling the dead despite my protests.

HospitalVisitCheck2.10.full: At one juncture, Dr. {0} approached a patient in the hallway that had been confined to a bath chair. Unprompted, they began a through examination of the individual, palpating their hairline and skull with their fingers. To my dismay, they were enraptured by a rash along the patients cheek which was covered in small protusions and red boils. They insisted on collecting several samples of the fluid they produced.
HospitalVisitCheck2.10.easy: At one point, Dr. {0} went up to a patient in a wheelchair in the corridor. Without asking, they started to examine the person closely and felt their hairline and skull with their fingers. To my horror, they were fascinated by a rash on the patient's cheek, full of small bumps and red boils. They insisted on taking several samples of the liquid that came out of them.
HospitalVisitCheck2.10.short: In a hallway, Dr. {0} examined a patient's skull uninvited, then, enraptured by a boil-covered rash, insisted on sampling its fluid.

HospitalVisitCheck2.11.full: After requesting access to more severe emergency cases, we walked the grounds. They kept stating that the facilities were "unimpressive compared to their own." I shudder to think on what that phrase means.
HospitalVisitCheck2.11.easy: After they asked to see more serious emergency cases, we walked around the grounds. They kept saying the hospital was "unimpressive compared to their own." I am afraid to think about what that means.
HospitalVisitCheck2.11.short: They called the facilities "unimpressive compared to their own." I shudder to think what that means.

HospitalVisitReject.2.full: Legal proceedings were still ongoing due to their previous visit to the Hospital grounds. HospitalVisitReject.2.short: With legal proceedings from their last visit still ongoing, Dr. {0} was unwelcome; their cousins watched them shout and try to force their way in.

HospitalVisitReject.3.full: Was it madness that drove them to it or a deep obsession that even this humble biographer cannot fathom? Whatever mental deficiency urged them onward, it certainly did not have the desired outcome.

HospitalVisitReject.3.short: Madness or obsession? Whatever drove them, it failed.

MWCompleteHubD.2.short: At midnight, lightning surged through the machinery. My creation awoke and gazed at me with wild eyes. I had created life!

MWCompleteHubD.3.full: To see my work in the flesh, to see {0} finally realized; the passion of the moment overwhelmed my senses. I had done it. I shook my fist at God and all who doubted me! You were wrong! I am invincible!
MWCompleteHubD.3.easy: To see my work in real life, to see {0} finally made real: the strong feelings of the moment were too much for me. I had done it. I shook my fist at God and at everyone who doubted me! You were wrong! Nobody can defeat me!

MWCompleteHubD.5.short: I squeezed the trigger. When the dust settled and my laboratory wall was gone, I grinned. The world would remember this weapon, and me.

MWCompleteHubD.6.short: The liquid swirled and glowed. The {0} was a stunning success; mass-produced, it would secure our legacy. My laughter echoed through my estate for years.

CreepyStar.2.full: As many found solace in drink and the blackening of the liver, this alcoholic inebriety soon devolved into open displays of unfounded accusations against those who displayed even a modest bit of intellect. They took a sense of malformed pride in the depths of their ignorance.
CreepyStar.2.easy: Many people looked for comfort in alcohol, which damaged their livers. Their drunkenness soon turned into open, unfair accusations against anyone who seemed even a little bit clever. They were strangely proud of how ignorant they were.
CreepyStar.2.short: Drink soon turned to baseless accusations against anyone with a modest intellect. They took pride in their ignorance.

CreepyStar.3.full: The reputation of a famed scientist, however mild in its influence over the scholars in Budapest, was firmly reviled by the faith-driven townsfolk. It was an easy target to blame their misfortunes upon. They would spit on the ground and whisper curses under their breath as the best known of the family walked by.
CreepyStar.3.easy: A famous scientist had only a little influence over the scholars in Budapest, but the religious townspeople strongly hated them. It was easy to blame them for all their bad luck. When the best-known members of the family walked past, the people spat on the ground and whispered curses.
CreepyStar.3.short: The faithful townsfolk reviled the famed scientists and blamed them for their woes, spitting and cursing as the family walked by.

CreepyStar.4.full: The player(s) with the most victory points immediately **gains 2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}**.

RippedMasterwork.2.full: In their late years, watching the town forsake science and wary colleagues abandon them, the weight of the injustice was all too much to bear. With fists raised to the sky, cursing the gods, they ended the generation in desperation!
RippedMasterwork.2.easy: In their old age, they watched the town turn away from science and careful colleagues leave them. This injustice was too much to bear. They raised their fists to the sky, cursed the gods, and ended the generation in despair!
RippedMasterwork.2.short: In old age, forsaken by the town and their colleagues, they shook their fists at the gods and ended the generation in desperation!

RippedMasterwork.3.full: The records of this time do not mention any notes of collaboration, yet each individual experienced their own bout of isolation and self-destructive mania. In a rage, they stormed their laboratories and each shattered retort, each biological anomaly encased in formaldehyde, each rusted contraption that met its end against the concrete floor was a new moment of catharsis.
RippedMasterwork.3.easy: The records from this time say nothing about working together, but each of them had their own time of loneliness and self-destructive madness. In anger, they rushed into their laboratories. Every broken glass vessel, every strange biological sample in formaldehyde, every rusty machine that broke on the concrete floor made them feel a little better.
RippedMasterwork.3.short: Each, alone, fell into self-destructive mania. They stormed their laboratories, and every shattered retort and smashed contraption brought catharsis.

RippedMasterwork.4.full: They held in their hands the feeble-minded schematic passed down from generation to generation, haunting them with its unattainable scientific pursuits, and unceremoniously scattered the torn pages across the floor.
RippedMasterwork.4.easy: They held the foolish plan in their hands that had been passed down from generation to generation. Its impossible scientific goals had haunted them. They tore it up and threw the pages on the floor.
RippedMasterwork.4.short: They tore up the inherited schematic, with its unattainable goals, and scattered the pages.

RippedMasterwork.5.full: Finally, they we were free from this cursed legacy!
RippedMasterwork.5.easy: At last they were free from this cursed legacy!
RippedMasterwork.5.short: Free at last from this cursed legacy!

S5HospA2.2.full: **With the University built,** the town slowly embraced the advances of modern science. But, while progress certainly had its benefits, it was unclear if these surprisingly mediocre "mad" scientists were prepared for the changes that lay just ahead in a world of fairness and social change.
S5HospA2.2.easy: **With the University built,** the town slowly accepted modern science. But progress had its good sides, and it was not clear if these surprisingly average "mad" scientists were ready for the changes that were coming: a world of fairness and social change.
S5HospA2.2.short: **With the University built,** the town slowly embraced science. But were these mediocre "mad" scientists ready for a world of fairness and social change?

S5HospA2.5.full: **With the University unbuilt,** the townsfolk were swayed by the local diocese to shun the sciences and cling to their faith. A swathe of ignorance encompassed the small town, as they moved towards a simpler time with simpler solutions.
S5HospA2.5.easy: **With the University unbuilt,** the local church convinced the townspeople to turn away from science and hold on to their faith. Ignorance spread over the small town, and it went back to a simpler time with simpler answers.
S5HospA2.5.short: **With the University unbuilt,** the church turned the town from science back to faith and simpler times.

Immortality, the likes of which the scientists craved, could never be sustained forever without some great sacrifice. Their continued existence was like a rolling of the dice, a gamble as precarious {0}
DetEffectRandom.4.easy: It is impossible to say it too strongly: it is dangerous to go against God and the natural order of things. The kind of immortality the scientists wanted could never last forever without some great sacrifice. Every day they lived was like throwing dice, a gamble as risky {0}
DetEffectRandom.4.short: Defying God and nature is dangerous; immortality demands sacrifice. Their existence was a roll of the dice, as precarious {0}

PanaceaIntro.2.full: Were they still not satisfied? The family pondered this as they enjoyed their morning tea on the veranda, peering over the countryside from behind their gothic spires while their experimentations simmered in the laboratories deep in their manors. The people, the scientists, the church; which institution would be the next to take exception to their important discoveries?
PanaceaIntro.2.easy: Were people still not happy? The family thought about this while they drank their morning tea on the terrace, looking over the countryside from behind their gothic towers, while their experiments bubbled in the laboratories deep inside their houses. The people, the scientists, the church: who would be the next to complain about their important discoveries?
PanaceaIntro.2.short: Over morning tea on the veranda, their experiments simmering below, the family wondered: who would object to their discoveries next?

PanaceaIntro.3.full: A Cure-All, or Grecian Panacea, became the newest topic of considerable divisiveness. It was the logical next step. Some in the family dismissed it as a waste of energy, while others valued it as a sought-after proposition.
PanaceaIntro.3.easy: A Cure-All, or Greek Panacea (a medicine against every illness), became the newest topic they strongly disagreed about. It was the logical next step. Some in the family said it was a waste of energy, others thought it was very much worth doing.
PanaceaIntro.3.short: A Cure-All, or Grecian Panacea, was the logical next step, and divided the family.

35VP.4.short: Their letters reveal a deep rivalry born of inadequacy, solitude and betrayal, at its worst when they sabotaged each other's work.

GloomyHunterIntro.3.full: The disease had revealed a much deeper evil than the family could have ever expected: An evil ignorance that dwells within the minds of the people. It had not only left the previous generation in shambles, but imbued the townsfolk with a profound, insatiable fear, even as the town returned to relative stability. During the day, the people watched the forests, glimpsing dark shadows flitting between the trees. At night, they steeled themselves against the wailing howls of unseen terrors, dreading that their children would be stolen away from their beds.
GloomyHunterIntro.3.easy: The disease had shown a much deeper evil than the family had ever expected: a dark ignorance in people's minds. It had destroyed the last generation, and it had filled the townspeople with a deep fear that never ended, even when life in town became more normal again. During the day, people watched the forests and saw dark shadows moving quickly between the trees. At night, they listened in fear to the howls of creatures they could not see, afraid that their children would be taken from their beds.
GloomyHunterIntro.3.short: The disease had revealed a deeper evil: ignorance. Even as the town recovered, fear ruled. By day, shadows flitted between the trees; by night, unseen things howled, and parents feared for their children.

GloomyHunterIntro.4.full: That was until the Fraternity of Hunters, emboldened by the success of their clandestine operations, emerged from the shadows on the night of a blood red moon. They wore long-tail coats of black, burgundy, and dark leather, a wooden cross hanging either from their necks or dangling from their sides. They clutched crossbows, whips, and daggers freshly glimmering with crimson fluid. Their blood-stained attire and steel-eyed gaze evoked the undaunted presence of ones who had peered into the void and returned forever changed.
GloomyHunterIntro.4.easy: That changed when the Fraternity of Hunters, made bold by the success of their secret work, came out of the shadows on the night of a blood-red moon. They wore long coats of black, dark red and dark leather, with a wooden cross around their necks or at their sides. They held crossbows, whips and daggers that were still shining with fresh red blood. Their bloody clothes and hard eyes showed people who had looked into the darkness and come back changed forever.
GloomyHunterIntro.4.short: Then, under a blood red moon, the Fraternity of Hunters emerged: long dark coats, wooden crosses, crossbows, whips and bloodied daggers. Their eyes had looked into the void.

GloomyHunterIntro.5.full: Their stated goal: to slay every last beast in the land and return those who had unleashed this foul plague back to the depths of hell from whence they came. The Fraternity turned the fear of the populace to their advantage. They fed the superstitions of the people, blaming the sickness and disease on fiendish creatures from the dark.
GloomyHunterIntro.5.easy: They said their goal was to kill every last beast in the land, and to send those who had started this terrible plague back to hell, where they came from. The Fraternity used the people's fear for its own purposes. They made the people's superstitions stronger and blamed the sickness and disease on evil creatures from the darkness.
GloomyHunterIntro.5.short: They vowed to slay every beast and send those who unleashed the plague back to hell. Feeding the people's superstitions, they blamed the disease on fiends from the dark.

GloomyHunterIntro.6.full: As expected, the family quickly grew to find their presence exhausting, both ideologically and financially. Clearly, the cousins opined, these Hunters' fear-mongering stemmed from a lack of true, scientific knowledge. As defenders against an unknown terror, they stood in direct competition to continued experimentation unfettered by ethical considerations. Yet, the Fraternity's need for additional capital to fuel their frequent "hunts" prevented the family from taking more direct action.
GloomyHunterIntro.6.easy: As expected, the family soon found the Hunters tiring, both because of their ideas and because of their cost. The cousins thought that the Hunters spread fear only because they had no real scientific knowledge. As defenders against an unknown danger, they stood in the way of experiments without any moral limits. But the Fraternity always needed more money for their frequent "hunts", and this stopped the family from acting against them more directly.
GloomyHunterIntro.6.short: The family soon found the Hunters exhausting, ideologically and financially. Their fear-mongering, the cousins felt, came from ignorance, and stood in the way of unfettered experimentation. Yet the Fraternity's hunger for funds kept the family from acting.

GloomyHunterIntro.7.full: Perhaps driven by a sense of limited time or jealousy over the Hunter's ability to frighten the townsfolk even moreso than their own actions, the cousins continued their meticulous labors in earnest. However, they were deeply unaware of just how intertwined their fates would be to the Fraternity.
GloomyHunterIntro.7.easy: Maybe because they felt time was running out, or because they were jealous that the Hunters could frighten the townspeople even more than they could, the cousins went on with their careful work with new energy. But they had no idea how closely their future would be connected to the Fraternity.
GloomyHunterIntro.7.short: Pressed for time, or jealous of the Hunters' power to frighten, the cousins worked on, unaware how bound their fates were to the Fraternity.

EvilConsequences.2.full: In the evenings, the Fraternity gathered in the former Town Hall and celebrated their political takeover of the small town. Observers could hear their loud revelry echo through the streets late into the night. The townsfolk had no reason to doubt their loyalty as it appeared that their activities kept both sickness and superstitions at bay.
EvilConsequences.2.easy: In the evenings, the Fraternity met in the old Town Hall and celebrated that they now ruled the small town. People could hear their loud parties in the streets until late at night. The townspeople had no reason to doubt them, because it seemed that the Fraternity kept away both sickness and superstition.
EvilConsequences.2.short: Each evening the Fraternity celebrated its takeover in the former Town Hall. The townsfolk trusted them: sickness and superstition stayed at bay.

EvilConsequences.3.full: For the family members that had aided them in their efforts, they wore wide false-smiles and offered toasts to their continued partnership. But, for those that had plotted against them, they remained wary.
EvilConsequences.3.easy: To the family members who had helped them, they gave big, false smiles and drank to their future partnership. But they stayed careful with those who had plotted against them.
EvilConsequences.3.short: They toasted the family members who had helped them, with false smiles, and watched those who had plotted against them.

EvilConsequences.4.full: In the center of town, in the full light of day and without fear of reprisal, a silver-haired beast rose to its hindlegs, almost human in stature. On the steps of the former Town Hall, she held the still-beating heart of a man who had refused to join their numbers.
EvilConsequences.4.easy: In the middle of town, in full daylight and without any fear of punishment, a silver-haired beast stood up on its back legs, almost as tall as a human. On the steps of the old Town Hall, she held the still-beating heart of a man who had refused to join them.
EvilConsequences.4.short: In broad daylight, on the steps of the former Town Hall, a silver-haired beast held aloft the still-beating heart of a man who had refused to join them.

EvilConsequences.5.full: The Order had revealed its true self with an unsettling ease, swiftly taking over the town and demanding alliance in the most vicious of terms. Streaks of dried blood and viscera adorned the windows of local businesses and homes. The family was only spared their wrath through allegiance or a cursed acknowledgement of their continued exploitation.
EvilConsequences.5.easy: The Order had shown its true face with frightening ease. It quickly took over the town and demanded loyalty with terrible threats. Lines of dried blood and guts covered the windows of local shops and houses. The family only escaped their anger by being loyal to them, or by accepting, as a curse, that they would go on being used.
EvilConsequences.5.short: The Order took the town with unsettling ease, demanding allegiance; blood and viscera streaked its windows. The family was spared only through loyalty, or by accepting continued exploitation.
