The Hunters were treated to a tickertape parade and glorious feast. But, as the light of the afternoon slowly faded, the sky began to glow with fiery intensity, and the revelry ceased.
HunterConfrontation.2.easy: After years of excuses and delays by the **Fraternity of Hunters**, the night of the Grand Contest had come. People all over the region had heard about the contest, and visitors came to the {0} Lodge to watch the hunt. The Hunters got a parade and a great feast. But as the afternoon light slowly faded, the sky began to glow like fire, and the party stopped.
HunterConfrontation.2.short: After years of delays by the **Fraternity of Hunters**, the Grand Contest arrived. Crowds gathered at the {0} Lodge for parade and feast, until the sky began to glow like fire.

HunterConfrontation.3.full: The Hunters donned their signature clothes, took up their well-polished arms, and proceeded down the main thoroughfare while the crimson light of the blood moon heralded their exit into the forests beyond.
HunterConfrontation.3.easy: The Hunters put on their famous clothes, took their polished weapons and marched down the main street, while the red light of the blood moon showed them the way into the forests.
HunterConfrontation.3.short: Armed and in their signature coats, the Hunters marched into the forests under the blood moon.

HunterConfrontation.4.full: That same fire reflected in the eyes of the scientists as they stifled their grim laughter. The night before, the cousins had prepared their chosen Experiments to release into the wild. It was time now for the Hunters to become the prey!
HunterConfrontation.4.easy: The same fire shone in the eyes of the scientists as they tried not to laugh darkly. The night before, the cousins had prepared their chosen Experiments to let them loose in the wild. Now it was time for the Hunters to become the hunted!
HunterConfrontation.4.short: The scientists stifled grim laughter. The night before, they had released their chosen Experiments. The Hunters would become the prey!

OhYesTheyDead.2.full: The cousins enjoyed fresh pastries and coffee as they admired the town's activities with amusement from their folding lawn chairs. When the triumphant return they had expected never came, the gathered crowds became restless and burst into the Hunter's Lodge only to discover stores of freshly slaughtered goat's blood and taxidermy supplies. The Fraternity had played them for fools.
OhYesTheyDead.2.easy: From their folding garden chairs, the cousins ate fresh pastries, drank coffee and watched the town with amusement. When the Hunters' victorious return that people expected never came, the crowd became restless and broke into the Hunter's Lodge. There they found supplies of fresh goat's blood and equipment for stuffing dead animals. The Fraternity had made fools of them.
OhYesTheyDead.2.short: The cousins watched with pastries and coffee. When no triumphant return came, the crowd stormed the Hunter's Lodge, finding goat's blood and taxidermy supplies. The Fraternity had played them for fools.

OhYesTheyDead.3.full: The town gallows had fallen into disrepair over the years, but upon the return of the remaining wild-eyed hunters that somehow survived the vicious experiments, lumber was quickly procured by the decidedly unimpressed townsfolk along with fresh hemp rope, thick and strong. The same crowd that gathered that afternoon for the festivities would be the crowd that watched every last writhing body swing lifeless for their crimes. If any Hunters did survive, they most certainly never returned.
OhYesTheyDead.3.easy: The town's gallows had been in bad condition for years. But when the last wild-eyed hunters who had somehow survived the terrible experiments came back, the very unhappy townspeople quickly brought wood and new, thick, strong rope. The same crowd that had come for the festival that afternoon watched every last body twist and then hang lifeless for their crimes. If any Hunters survived, they certainly never came back.
OhYesTheyDead.3.short: The townsfolk mended the gallows with fresh rope, and the crowd that came to celebrate watched every surviving Hunter hang. If any escaped, they never returned.

OhYesTheyDead.4.full: The people would speak of the Grand Contest as one of the crowning events in the history of {0}. Having rooted out the evil infesting their government, the town entered a period of peace that was especially productive for a group of scientists.
OhYesTheyDead.4.easy: People would talk about the Grand Contest as one of the greatest events in the history of {0}. After they had removed the evil in their government, the town had a time of peace, which was very productive for a certain group of scientists.
OhYesTheyDead.4.short: The Grand Contest became a high point in the history of {0}. Its government cleansed of evil, the town entered a peace most productive for certain scientists.

Educated middle-class families strolled along the sidewalks in modest clothing. Children laughed and rode bicycles in the park. They shuddered at the sight. It was all **too good**.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.2.easy: The {0} cousins watched with heavy hearts as the once gloomy streets were decorated with bright spring colors. Educated middle-class families walked along the sidewalks in simple clothes. Children laughed and rode bicycles in the park. The cousins shivered at the sight. It was all **too good**.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.2.short: The {0} cousins watched glumly as the streets bloomed with color, families strolled and children laughed. They shuddered. It was all **too good**.

UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.3.full: With the initial festivities over, their estimation had soured in the eyes of the academics. Though they had not been spurned or mistreated, the once generous enthusiasm had waned from repeated ethical infractions, misuse of the medical operating theater, and radical outbursts during local symposiums. And to complicate matters further, it became increasingly obvious that due to the peaceful and progressive values of {0}, the educated were less troubled with matters of any immediate, existential, or diabolical concern.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.3.easy: After the first celebrations, the academics thought less of them. Nobody rejected them or treated them badly, but the once warm enthusiasm had faded because of many moral violations, wrong use of the operating room and wild outbursts at local symposiums. To make it worse, it became more and more clear that because {0} was so peaceful and progressive, educated people no longer worried much about any urgent, life-threatening or devilish problems.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.3.short: The academics' enthusiasm had waned after ethical infractions, misuse of the operating theater and outbursts at symposiums. Worse, peaceful, progressive {0} had no urgent, existential or diabolical concerns left.

UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.4.full: The solution to this lack of a problem was obvious. If the world refused to create a new, horrific problem to solve, then they would defy nature and create it themselves. Surely, if they combined their efforts, they could create the **ultimate disease**! A disease so infectious that they would forever undo this plague of positivity.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.4.easy: The answer to this lack of problems was clear. If the world would not create a new, terrible problem to solve, they would go against nature and create one themselves. Surely, if they worked together, they could create the **ultimate disease**! A disease so infectious that it would end this plague of positivity forever.
UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.4.short: The solution was obvious: if the world would not create a horrific problem, they would. Together, they would make the **ultimate disease**, and end this plague of positivity!

UniEvent1-UltimateDisease.5.full: This would certainly **rid them of this unfair and blatant balancing** of fortunes.

UniEvent2-Success.2.full: Symptoms: Nausea, fever, vomiting, hypertension, drowsiness, loss of libido, skin lesions, blurred vision, heart palpitations, headache, weight-loss, chronic pain, demonic possession. The prospectus for the ultimate disease included nearly every side-effect known to science. The cousins spent the late-night hours laughing till their throats were hoarse as they concocted the elixir.
UniEvent2-Success.2.easy: Symptoms: feeling sick, fever, vomiting, high blood pressure, sleepiness, loss of sexual desire, skin wounds, blurred vision, a racing heart, headache, weight loss, long-lasting pain, possession by demons. The plan for the ultimate disease included almost every side effect known to science. The cousins laughed late into the night until their throats were sore while they mixed the potion.
UniEvent2-Success.2.short: Symptoms: nausea, fever, vomiting, lesions, palpitations, chronic pain, demonic possession, and nearly every other side-effect known to science. The cousins laughed themselves hoarse brewing it.

UniEvent2-Success.3.full: The following week, the disease was released at the Farmer's Market, a tincture of the foul liquid smashed against the steps. It proved communicable within seconds and the noxious gases spread from person-to-person with each dry cough.
UniEvent2-Success.3.easy: The next week, they released the disease at the Farmer's Market: a small bottle of the disgusting liquid was smashed on the steps. Within seconds it was spreading, and the poisonous gases passed from person to person with every dry cough.
UniEvent2-Success.3.short: The next week, a vial smashed on the Farmer's Market steps. Within seconds, it spread with every dry cough.

UniEvent2-Success.4.full: However, the effect was not altogether anticipated. This grim amalgamation of deadly diseases, while invoking minor symptoms in some initially exposed, caused antibodies to build up within the region, nullifying their effects and strengthening their systems against infection. By creating a disease that included all known symptoms, they had essentially inoculated the populace against all disease simultaneously.
UniEvent2-Success.4.easy: But the result was not quite what they expected. This dark mix of deadly diseases gave some of the first people only small symptoms. But it made antibodies grow in the whole region, which stopped the effects and made people's bodies stronger against infection. By creating a disease with all known symptoms, they had basically vaccinated everyone against all diseases at the same time.
UniEvent2-Success.4.short: But instead of ravaging the town, it built up antibodies. A disease with every symptom had inoculated the populace against all disease at once.

UniEvent2-Success.5.full: It wasn't long before the university traced the source of the marvel to the cousins. Word soon traveled about their research, and the town applauded yet another triumph for science and the world! Clearly, this family of scientists needed no assistance in their heavenly endeavors.
UniEvent2-Success.5.easy: Soon the university found out that this wonder came from the cousins. The news about their research spread quickly, and the town celebrated one more success for science and for the world! Clearly, this family of scientists needed no help with their wonderful work.
UniEvent2-Success.5.short: The university traced the marvel to the cousins, and the town celebrated another triumph for science. Clearly, this family needed no assistance!

UniEvent2-Failure.2.easy: The cousins kept their knowledge to themselves and could not agree on what to do next, so the meeting soon turned into arguing and trying to be better than each other. Each cousin talked for a long time about their own successes and about how jealous the others secretly were of their work. Many of the pastries were left half-eaten that night.
UniEvent2-Failure.2.short: Guarding their knowledge, the cousins fell to bickering and boasting. Many pastries were left half-eaten.

MayoralAward.4.short: The townsfolk credited {0} III's line with championing **knowledge** for generations, and wish to repay these Librarians.

MayoralAward.5.full: Retrieve the **Personal Library** Estate Upgrade from the scenario box. You may immediately build it in the next empty plot on your Estate board at no additional cost. Then, return the **Commemorative Mayoral Coin** to the box.

MayoralAward.6.full: Whenever you take the Perform Experiment action, the **Personal Library** provides one free Knowledge of your choice from the supply. This Knowledge can be used immediately towards the cost of Performing that Experiment.

HunterJoin.2.full: A messenger arrives at sunset wearing a pendant around their neck with a golden bow and arrow insignia upon it. They wait expectantly for your correspondence.
HunterJoin.2.easy: A messenger comes at sunset, wearing a pendant around their neck with a golden bow and arrow on it. They wait for your answer.
HunterJoin.2.short: At sunset, a messenger with a golden bow-and-arrow pendant awaits your answer.

HunterJoin.3.full: Pledge your service to the Fraternity of Hunters.

RefusalEvent.2.full: As the black carriage approached, the young man paused in his duties and lit a small pipe. In these dark times, a stablehand knew more about the comings and goings of the townsfolk than most anyone in the region. A few conspiratorial words and he was generous with information.
RefusalEvent.2.easy: When the black carriage came closer, the young man stopped working and lit a small pipe. In these dark times, a stable boy knew more about who came and went in town than almost anyone in the region. After a few secret words, he was happy to share what he knew.
RefusalEvent.2.short: The young stable hand paused and lit a pipe. Few knew more about the town's comings and goings, and a few words loosened his tongue.

JoinedAlready.2.full: The man looked at {0} quizzically for a moment before shaking his head and returning to work. {1} had already joined a faction and continued on their way after the fog cleared from their mind.
JoinedAlready.2.easy: The man looked at {0} with confusion for a moment, then shook his head and went back to work. {1} had already joined a faction, and went on their way when their head was clear again.
JoinedAlready.2.short: The man shook his head at {0} and returned to work. {1} had already joined a faction, and moved on.

EquitableValues.2.full: For the first time in decades, the townsfolk expressed a sense of community, a singular and modern identity.
EquitableValues.2.easy: For the first time in decades, the townspeople felt like a community, with one shared, modern identity.
EquitableValues.2.short: For the first time in decades, the town felt like a community.

EquitableValues.3.full: The Order of St. Hubertus remained an official moniker, but a new, more democratic society emerged. The secrets that had remained hidden for so long had finally been exposed and the sense of freedom was finally something worth protecting.
EquitableValues.3.easy: The Order of St. Hubertus kept its official name, but a new, more democratic society was born. The secrets that had been hidden for so long were finally exposed, and freedom was finally something worth protecting.
EquitableValues.3.short: The Order of St. Hubertus kept its name, but a more democratic society emerged. With the secrets exposed, freedom was worth protecting.

EquitableValues.4.full: While members of the Fraternity attended to their dark business, sharpening their skills and weapons on their own, the town remained resolute in their ability to rid the surrounding hills of evil.
EquitableValues.4.easy: While members of the Fraternity did their dark work and trained their skills and weapons alone, the town was sure that it could free the hills around it from evil.
EquitableValues.4.short: While the Fraternity sharpened its weapons alone, the town resolved to rid the hills of evil itself.

EquitableValues.5.full: Unlike previous generations that were keen to allow an aloof eccentric to isolate themselves amongst the rocky crags at the valley's edge, the townsfolk became determined in their attempts to ingratiate the obstinate cousins into the fold. While the reception was always cold and the iron gates and foreboding wooden doorways were mostly closed to them, they never stopped trying.
EquitableValues.5.easy: Earlier generations had been happy to let a strange, distant person live alone in the rocks at the edge of the valley. But these townspeople were determined to make the stubborn cousins part of the community. The answer was always cold, and the iron gates and dark wooden doors were usually closed to them, but they never stopped trying.
EquitableValues.5.short: Unlike past generations, the townsfolk tried to win over the obstinate cousins. The gates mostly stayed shut, but they never stopped trying.

EquitableValues.6.full: While they would never admit to it, the ones who were most desperate tended to accept the offers more readily.
EquitableValues.6.easy: They would never admit it, but the cousins who needed it most usually said yes more easily.
EquitableValues.6.short: Though none would admit it, the most desperate accepted most readily.

EquitableValues.8.full: player with the fewest VP gains 1

EquitableValues.9.full: **2** players with the fewest VP gain 1

EquitableValues.10.full: of their Servants from Lost. *Ties are broken by the player who went last in the previous round.*

EquitableValues.11.full: The player with the most points gains 2 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.

LycanMessageGood.2.full: Though the sight had now become commonplace, confirming the existence of persons with the ability to change into an animal form had remarkable consequences. It is possible that it even disrupted the studies of one of our kin.
LycanMessageGood.2.easy: It was now a normal sight, but proving that some people can change into an animal had great consequences. It may even have disturbed the studies of one of our family.
LycanMessageGood.2.short: Now a common sight, proof of shapeshifters still had great consequences, perhaps even for one of our kin's studies.

LycanMessageGood.3.full: Does any player have the **Lycanthropic Strength** Masterwork Experiment?

WolvesEco-Friendly.2.full: As the new decade began, the motley parade of beastly horrors had turned their claws from weapons of destruction into instruments of cultivation. They embraced modern amenities and fashions, walking the streets with upright strides as the town continued to thrive.
WolvesEco-Friendly.2.easy: When the new decade began, the colorful crowd of beastly horrors had turned their claws from weapons into tools for farming. They liked modern comforts and fashions, and walked upright through the streets as the town went on growing.
WolvesEco-Friendly.2.short: In the new decade, the beasts turned their claws to cultivation, embracing modern fashions and walking upright through the thriving town.

WolvesEco-Friendly.3.full: For most, however, this new sense of peace was tarnished by the persistence of past injustices. As newspaper pressings became even more accessible, pamphlets and signage began to circulate amongst the populace.
WolvesEco-Friendly.3.easy: But for most of them, this new peace was spoiled because they could not forget old injustices. As newspapers became easier to print, leaflets and signs started to go around town.
WolvesEco-Friendly.3.short: But old injustices lingered, and pamphlets began to circulate.

WolvesEco-Friendly.4.full: "Our brethren; abused, slaughtered, and experimented upon. No more! We can bear this injustice no longer." One paper stated, "Meat is murder."
WolvesEco-Friendly.4.easy: "Our brothers and sisters: hurt, killed and used for experiments. No more! We cannot accept this injustice any longer." One paper said: "Meat is murder."
WolvesEco-Friendly.4.short: "Our brethren, slaughtered and experimented upon. No more!" One paper stated, "Meat is murder."

WolvesEco-Friendly.5.full: Most had adopted a Pythagorean diet, developing a keen culinary taste for vegetable curries and rich, barley porridge. While it was not strictly forbidden to consume the cooked flesh of domestic animals, when the cousins' town business included a stop by the Farmer's Market, the townsfolk looked away in horror, mothers shielding their furred children's eyes as the implication was too much for them to bear.
WolvesEco-Friendly.5.easy: Most of them now ate no meat and had learned to love vegetable curries and rich barley porridge. Eating cooked farm animals was not really forbidden, but when the cousins' business in town included a visit to the Farmer's Market, the townspeople looked away in horror, and mothers covered the eyes of their furry children, because the thought was too much for them.
WolvesEco-Friendly.5.short: Most now ate vegetable curries and barley porridge. When the cousins visited the Farmer's Market, mothers covered their furry children's eyes in horror.

WolvesEco-Friendly.6.full: Yet still roiling beneath the thin veneer of prim etiquette, a baser nature threatened to reemerge anew.
WolvesEco-Friendly.6.easy: But under their thin, polite good manners, a wilder nature was still bubbling and could come back at any time.
WolvesEco-Friendly.6.short: Yet beneath the prim etiquette, a baser nature stirred.

WolvesEco-Friendly.7.full: Put a {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Farmer's Market**.

AngryMobStorybook.2.full: There were moments when the rage amongst the townsfolk would well up and explode in uncontrollably violent outbursts. For the monsters of {0}, these were no longer represented by torches or pitchforks held high, but by a feverish bloodlust.
AngryMobStorybook.2.easy: Sometimes the anger of the townspeople grew until it exploded in violence they could not control. For the monsters of {0}, this no longer meant torches or pitchforks held high, but a wild hunger for blood.
AngryMobStorybook.2.short: At times the townsfolk's rage exploded. For the monsters of {0}, that meant not torches and pitchforks, but bloodlust.

AngryMobStorybook.3.full: As such, it was a calm Sunday afternoon when a local werewolf doffed his cap and interrupted tea time by holding up a blood-stained and torn piece of fabric.
AngryMobStorybook.3.easy: So on a quiet Sunday afternoon, a local werewolf took off his cap and interrupted tea time by holding up a bloody, torn piece of cloth.
AngryMobStorybook.3.short: One Sunday, a werewolf interrupted tea, holding up a torn, bloodied scrap of fabric.

AngryMobStorybook.4.full: He placed the scrap onto the table. "We would return the body to you for proper burial if it were still possible," he shrugged, his ears flattening. "But, you know how it goes when bones are involved. Sorry."
AngryMobStorybook.4.easy: He put the piece of cloth on the table. "We would give you the body back for a proper funeral if we could," he said with a shrug, his ears going flat. "But you know what happens when there are bones. Sorry."
AngryMobStorybook.4.short: "We'd return the body for burial if we could," he shrugged, ears flat. "But you know how it goes with bones. Sorry."

AngryMobStorybook.5.full: Another good servant gone. It was somewhat inevitable, yet still an unfortunate loss of life, time and money.
AngryMobStorybook.5.easy: Another good servant lost. It was almost bound to happen, but it was still a sad loss of life, time and money.
AngryMobStorybook.5.short: Another good servant gone; an inevitable but costly loss.

AngryMobStorybook.6.full: To be awakened early morning after a late night's work was agitating, but to awake to a shrill, blood-curdling scream was something else entirely.
AngryMobStorybook.6.easy: Being woken up early in the morning after working late was annoying, but being woken up by a loud, terrible scream was something completely different.
AngryMobStorybook.6.short: Waking early after a late night was irritating; waking to a blood-curdling scream was another matter.

AngryMobStorybook.7.full: A woman in a modest blue dress crouched near the entrance to the estate, her blood-covered maw held within two clawed hands as she wailed in distress. A few feet away, two wolves clad in sharp business suits huddled over the dead body of a servant, tearing into the flesh with their teeth and claws as fresh blood flowed down the gravel drive.
AngryMobStorybook.7.easy: A woman in a simple blue dress was crouching near the entrance to the estate, holding her bloody mouth in her two clawed hands and crying in distress. A few steps away, two wolves in smart business suits were bent over the dead body of a servant, tearing the flesh with their teeth and claws while fresh blood ran down the gravel driveway.
AngryMobStorybook.7.short: A woman in blue crouched wailing at the gate, her maw bloodied. Nearby, two wolves in business suits tore into a dead servant on the gravel drive.

AngryMobStorybook.8.full: A monster stood nearby, clearly resisting the urge to join into the fray. He fixed his tie and wiped away saliva from his chin before speaking in a solemn voice. "Poor thing couldn't control herself. Took the first bite. Terrible tragedy. Awfully sorry."
AngryMobStorybook.8.easy: A monster stood nearby, clearly trying hard not to join in. He fixed his tie and wiped the spit from his chin before he spoke in a serious voice: "Poor thing couldn't control herself. Took the first bite. Terrible tragedy. Awfully sorry."
AngryMobStorybook.8.short: A monster nearby, resisting the urge to join, fixed his tie and wiped his chin. "Poor thing couldn't control herself. Took the first bite. Awfully sorry."

AngryMobStorybook.9.full: Perhaps it was unavoidable that the close proximity of humanity to the beasts would incite such an event.
AngryMobStorybook.9.easy: Maybe something like this had to happen when humans and beasts lived so close together.
AngryMobStorybook.9.short: Perhaps it was unavoidable, with humans and beasts so close.

AngryMobStorybook.12.full: Move your {icon:Creepy_Icon} token **2 spaces** to the left. Move the {icon:AngryMob_Icon} token **3 spaces** to the right *(or as far as possible)*.

GoodFrenzyEvent.2.full: While the system of progressive monster reform was altruistic, it was not without its imperfections. Infractions ranging from minor maulings to severe interdental jugular removal were noted over the years, as were the manic episodes associated with these incidents.
GoodFrenzyEvent.2.easy: The program to make the monsters better was well meant, but it was not perfect. Over the years, there were many incidents, from small bites to serious cases of throats being bitten out, and also the wild fits that came with them.
GoodFrenzyEvent.2.short: The monster reform program was well-meant but imperfect: over the years came maulings, torn-out jugulars and manic episodes.

GoodFrenzyEvent.3.full: It was clear that humans were marginally upset about the lack of livestock and uptick in missing persons potentially consumed by wolves. It was also clear that each monster would experience near daily urges to indulge in profane behavior that they were forced to suppress.
GoodFrenzyEvent.3.easy: Clearly, the humans were a little upset about the missing farm animals and the growing number of missing people who were possibly eaten by wolves. It was also clear that every monster felt, almost every day, a wish to do terrible things that they had to hold back.
GoodFrenzyEvent.3.short: Humans were somewhat upset about vanishing livestock and missing persons. And every monster fought near-daily urges they had to suppress.

GoodFrenzyEvent.4.full: Perhaps, they suggested, if they could attempt to indulge their darker urges in a safe space where this expression was fully encouraged, then it would pacify those urges at other more domestic times.
GoodFrenzyEvent.4.easy: Maybe, they suggested, if they could let out their darker wishes in a safe place where this was fully allowed, it would calm these wishes at other, more normal times.
GoodFrenzyEvent.4.short: Perhaps, they suggested, a safe space to indulge those urges would calm them at other times.

YesFrenzy.2.full: The townsfolk who chose not to participate locked their doors and boarded their windows, but the first howls of ghoulish delight sent those same individuals clawing at the walls to be released into the wild again. The Frenzy spared no person in {0}. The unhinged spectacle set the teeth gnashing and a passionate fire blazing both metaphorically and physically, plumes of hot embers erupting upwards from homes set ablaze with wild abandon. When a door burst open or a window shattered, barely a strangled cry could be heard before another victim's fresh blood spilled into the streets.
YesFrenzy.2.easy: The townspeople who did not want to take part locked their doors and nailed boards over their windows. But at the first howls of evil joy, these same people scratched at the walls to be let out into the wild again. The Frenzy spared nobody in {0}. The crazy scene made teeth grind and set a wild fire burning, in their hearts and for real: clouds of hot sparks rose from houses that were set on fire without any control. When a door broke open or a window smashed, you could hardly hear a choked cry before the fresh blood of another victim ran into the streets.
YesFrenzy.2.short: Those who stayed behind boarded their windows, but at the first howls they clawed to get out. The Frenzy spared no one in {0}. Homes burned, doors burst, and blood ran in the streets.

YesFrenzy.3.full: Indulging in latent urges proved not to quell the dormant urges of the citizenry, but to stoke it. In the coming weeks, the logical faculties of the changed townfolk were removed. And in its place, a well of anger and a bloodlust so acute it left the landscape to darken and the soil to sour!
YesFrenzy.3.easy: Giving in to their hidden wishes did not calm the sleeping wishes of the citizens; it made them stronger. In the following weeks, the changed townspeople lost their ability to think clearly. In its place came a deep anger and a hunger for blood so strong that the land grew dark and the soil went bad!
YesFrenzy.3.short: Indulgence did not quell the urges, it stoked them. Within weeks, reason gave way to rage and bloodlust that darkened the land and soured the soil!

YesFrenzy.4.full: The thin line between civility and savagery had been severed. The monsters were set loose to prowl the region and invoke their hideous reign upon the unsuspecting masses.
YesFrenzy.4.easy: The thin line between good manners and wildness was broken. The monsters were set free to hunt the region and rule over the unsuspecting people in a terrible way.
YesFrenzy.4.short: The line between civility and savagery was severed, and the monsters were loosed upon the region.

NoFrenzy.2.full: The recommendation was accepted with gravitas. While many remained wistful, the group's almost immediate adoption of the concept made it clearly a dangerous proposition.
NoFrenzy.2.easy: The suggestion was taken very seriously. Many were a little sad, but the group liked the idea almost at once, and this showed clearly how dangerous it was.
NoFrenzy.2.short: The recommendation was received gravely. That the group embraced it so quickly showed how dangerous it was.

NoFrenzy.3.full: To further preoccupy their minds and to quell the bloodlust just beneath the surface, they offered further building assistance to reinforce a wider variety of scientific disciplines.
NoFrenzy.3.easy: To keep their minds busy and to calm the hunger for blood just under the surface, they offered more help with buildings to support more different areas of science.
NoFrenzy.3.short: To occupy their minds and quell their bloodlust, they offered to help build for more scientific disciplines.

NoFrenzy.4.full: Retrieve the **Chemistry** and **Engineering Master's Study** Vanity Estate Upgrades from the scenario box and place them nearby. Any time you gain a Vanity Estate Upgrade, you may choose to gain 1 of these instead.

WolvesEvil2.2.full: The messenger did not appear until nightfall, whereupon the lateness of arrival interrupted the cousins' dessert and coffee. The moonlight reflected off his steel gaze as he entered the sitting room without invitation. His fangs had tasted blood that same night.
WolvesEvil2.2.easy: The messenger only came when it was dark, and because he came so late, he interrupted the cousins' dessert and coffee. The moonlight shone in his cold, hard eyes as he walked into the living room without being invited. His teeth had tasted blood that same night.
WolvesEvil2.2.short: The messenger arrived at nightfall, interrupting dessert. Moonlight glinted in his steel gaze as he entered uninvited, his fangs freshly bloodied.

WolvesEvil2.3.full: The family could delay their offering no longer and the beasts of the Order salivated with anticipation over the knowledge they would soon acquire.
WolvesEvil2.3.easy: The family could not wait any longer to give what they had promised, and the beasts of the Order were drooling with excitement about the knowledge they would soon get.
WolvesEvil2.3.short: The family could delay no longer, and the Order's beasts salivated over the knowledge to come.

WolvesEvil2.5.full: In turn order, each player decides whether to contribute an Experiment. Donated Experiments are turned face-down and placed under your Masterwork card.

WolvesEvil2.6.full: If a player donates, they will receive an immediate bonus based on the level of Experiment they donate (*higher levels granting higher rewards*).

WolvesEvil2.7.full: If a player chooses not to donate, they will **lose a Servant** and **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}**.

WolvesEvil2.8.full: Click here to receive bonuses and penalties...

Preparations-TCOD.2.full: Complete the standard setup for {0} players as shown in the rulebook. *Note that the {icon:AngryMob_Icon} track and starting player will be set by the Storybook in the coming pages.*

Preparations-TCOD.4.full: Then, retrieve **The Cost of Disease** Scenario box, which will contain all components needed for this story. As the Storybook progresses, it will ask you to put items into play from this box. Be sure to keep it nearby.

Preface-TCOD.2.full: Herein contains a historical account of a peculiar lineage. One that spans multiple generations and by all accounts will continue to fascinate historians for many years to come.
Preface-TCOD.2.easy: This book tells the true history of an unusual family. Their story covers many generations, and historians will find it interesting for many years to come.
Preface-TCOD.2.short: Herein lies the history of a peculiar lineage, one that will fascinate historians for generations.

Preface-TCOD.3.full: I have endeavored to provide as complete a scholarly history as one could provide given the conflicting accounts and whims of hearsay. While many of the details, haunting to the imagination as they may be, stretch the very limits of our human understanding, it is my hope that this text and the accompanying research materials procured will provide evidence as to their truth. The harrowing and potentially supernatural series of events has the capacity to shake the very foundations of the scientific world as we perceive it.
Preface-TCOD.3.easy: I have tried to make this history as complete as possible, even though people told different stories, and not all of them were true. Many details are frightening and hard to believe. But I hope that this book and the research that comes with it will show that they are true. These strange and perhaps supernatural events could change what science believes about our world.
Preface-TCOD.3.short: I have pieced this history together from conflicting accounts and hearsay. Its harrowing, perhaps supernatural events may shake the very foundations of science.

Preface-TCOD.4.full: With deference to the fellowship that commissioned this explicit work, though I have never met with these generous benefactors, I humbly submit this biographical account in its entirety and swear by the veracity of the contents within.
Preface-TCOD.4.easy: I have never met the group that asked me to write this book, but I thank them for their generous support. I humbly give them the whole story, and I promise that everything in it is true.
Preface-TCOD.4.short: To the generous fellowship that commissioned it, I humbly submit this account and swear to its truth.

Diseases2.2.full: When the symptoms grew too fierce, they locked themselves away inside one of the myriad rooms of their estate. This resulted in an unfortunate loss of productivity and an odiferous contamination. When chemicals would not suffice for cleansing, it was deemed necessary to burn the entire room and start again.
Diseases2.2.easy: When the symptoms became too strong, they locked themselves into one of the many rooms of their estate. This meant that they lost a lot of working time, and the room got a terrible smell. When chemicals could not clean it, they had to burn the whole room and start again.
Diseases2.2.short: When the symptoms grew fierce, they locked themselves away, losing work time. When chemicals could not clean the stench, the room was burned.

Diseases2.4.full: While the disease that plagued the scientists was manageable, the effects were still tiresome. Time spent advancing what they considered "true science" was instead squandered upon practical medical applications to assuage their own afflictions.
Diseases2.4.easy: The disease that troubled the scientists could be controlled, but its effects were still tiring. Instead of working on what they called "true science", they had to waste time on practical medicine to help with their own illness.
Diseases2.4.short: The disease was manageable but tiresome, wasting time on medicine for themselves instead of "true science".

Diseases2.5.full: All players that have not completed their **Hereditary Disease Experiment** must **discard an Estate Upgrade tile** to the box or **lose 3VP**.

Diseases2.6.full: All players that have not completed their **Hereditary Disease Experiment** must **lose 2VP**.

DiseaseEnd.2.full: Notes from this time period detail potential blueprints for a special room; a sanguine coagulant encased in a glass bubble and fed with an electrical current. Although there are no further mentions of the device, peculiarities in historical accounts suggest that some in the next generation received advice and assistance from an unknown source.
DiseaseEnd.2.easy: Notes from this time describe possible plans for a special room: a blood-clotting substance inside a glass bubble, powered by electricity. There is nothing more about this machine in the records, but some strange details in the history books suggest that some people in the next generation got advice and help from an unknown source.
DiseaseEnd.2.short: Notes describe plans for a special room: a blood coagulant in a glass bubble fed by electricity. Nothing more is recorded, but some in the next generation seem to have received help from an unknown source.

DiseaseEnd.3.full: Click here to determine the fate of the town...

WolfJoin.2.full: A messenger in a gray cloak marked with the insignia of a wolf's head arrived at the estate one evening. They smiled and the gleam of their white teeth shone in the moonlight.
WolfJoin.2.easy: One evening, a messenger in a gray cloak with the sign of a wolf's head arrived at the estate. They smiled, and their white teeth shone in the moonlight.
WolfJoin.2.short: One evening, a messenger in a gray wolf's-head cloak arrived, white teeth gleaming in the moonlight.

WolfJoin.3.full: Pledge your service to the Order of St. Hubertus.

Aside from the notoriety afforded by this gift, as promised, a permanent structure was to be erected on their properties to aid in their experimental pursuits.
HelpingEvil.2.easy: When the new Generation of scientists received their inheritance, they were surprised to find a generous extra gift from the {0}. As promised, besides the fame that came with this gift, a permanent building would be built on their land to help with their experiments.
HelpingEvil.2.short: With their inheritance came a generous addendum from the {0}: as promised, a permanent structure on their land to aid their experiments.

MWTokenResolve.2.full: The gathering of clawed monstrosities celebrated with keening wails as the Masterwork was completed in all of its glory. Surely, the legacy of the family would be secured forever. Yet, the watchful, glowing eyes of the crowd did not share this same deference to sentimentality.
MWTokenResolve.2.easy: The crowd of clawed monsters celebrated with high howls when the Masterwork was finished in all its glory. Surely, the family's legacy was now safe forever. But the watching, glowing eyes of the crowd did not share these warm feelings.
MWTokenResolve.2.short: The clawed crowd howled as the Masterwork was completed. The family's legacy seemed secure, but the glowing eyes watching did not share the sentiment.

MWTokenResolve.3.full: A furious cacophony of growls sounded as the monsters surrounded the experiment. Some scribbled away at notes, copying the formulas and schematics as best as they could while others simply traced every minute detail with their fingers and observed with interest.
MWTokenResolve.3.easy: With wild, loud growling, the monsters surrounded the experiment. Some quickly wrote notes and copied the formulas and plans as well as they could. Others just followed every small detail with their fingers and watched with interest.
MWTokenResolve.3.short: Growling, the monsters surrounded it, some copying formulas and schematics, others tracing every detail with their claws.

MWTokenResolve.4.full: It was clear that they would have been much more able to understand and reproduce the results of the experiment if they had been given earlier access to the cousin's work over the years.
MWTokenResolve.4.easy: It was clear that they could have understood and copied the results much better if they had seen the cousins' work earlier over the years.
MWTokenResolve.4.short: Earlier access to the cousins' work would clearly have helped them reproduce it.

MWTokenResolve.5.full: Resolve your Masterwork as normal. Then, for each Experiment under your Masterwork, **lose 4VP**. Discard all cards under your Masterwork.

Evilsforgive.2.full: The scientists' doubts were put at ease when a werewolf in a brown sack suit took to the podium to preside over a town meeting. A mixture of lycanthropic beings, horned beasts, and those still holding onto their humanity were in attendance outside the school. The force of the wolf's words caused tears to stream down their cheeks.

Evilsforgive.4.full: As a token of this myth-shattering event, many handshakes were exchanged that day and a promise was made to press forward into a more modern era; an era where science could improve their lives ten-fold!
Evilsforgive.4.easy: To mark this event, which proved the old myths wrong, people shook many hands that day and promised to move forward into a more modern time, a time when science could make their lives ten times better!
Evilsforgive.4.short: Hands were shaken, and a promise made: onward to a modern era where science would better their lives tenfold!

EvilWolvesEventStart.2.full: The Order of St. Hubertus' Lodge held a dark secret in the miasmic recesses beneath the edifice above, and after navigating a steep spiraling stone staircase, the cousins found themselves in a large stone room: a makeshift laboratory deep enough beneath the earth that the walls were warm with heat. Glass baubles and pilfered tools were stacked haphazardly around several wooden workspaces with failed experiments and devices thrown into metal waste bins beneath.
EvilWolvesEventStart.2.easy: The Lodge of the Order of St. Hubertus had a dark secret in the stinking rooms under the building. After going down a steep, winding stone staircase, the cousins found themselves in a large stone room: a homemade laboratory so deep under the ground that the walls were warm. Glass objects and stolen tools were piled up untidily around several wooden work tables, and failed experiments and machines had been thrown into metal bins underneath.
EvilWolvesEventStart.2.short: Beneath the Order of St. Hubertus' Lodge, down a spiraling stair, lay a laboratory so deep its walls were warm, cluttered with glassware, stolen tools and failed experiments.

EvilWolvesEventStart.3.full: The Lodge's caretaker extended a long clawed hand towards the center of the room, where a large circular stone well squatted. When they peered inside, they saw the infernal spawning grounds. Slime-covered beasts wallowed within a murky pit sloshing with the putrid stench of rotten meat. They wailed in unseen torment as the caretakers of the Order snapped coiled whips to frighten the malformed wretches into submission.
EvilWolvesEventStart.3.easy: The Lodge's caretaker pointed a long, clawed hand to the middle of the room, where there was a large round stone well. When they looked inside, they saw the hellish place where the creatures were born. Beasts covered in slime rolled around in a dark pit that stank of rotten meat. They cried in pain, as the Order's caretakers cracked whips to frighten the misshapen creatures into obeying.
EvilWolvesEventStart.3.short: The caretaker gestured to a stone well. Within, slime-covered beasts wallowed in a pit reeking of rot, wailing as the Order's whips cracked.

EvilWolvesEventStart.4.full: The caretaker spoke in a harsh, gravelly tone, "You are free to use this place as you wish. All that we ask is for a single experiment when we call upon you. Alternatively, our children here are always so very hungry."
EvilWolvesEventStart.4.easy: The caretaker spoke in a rough, harsh voice: "You may use this place as you like. All we ask is one experiment when we call on you. Or else, our children here are always very hungry."
EvilWolvesEventStart.4.short: "Use this place as you wish," the caretaker rasped. "We ask only one experiment when we call. Otherwise, our children are always so very hungry."

EvilWolvesEventStart.5.full: It was a dark boon indeed to be offered a place in town to **perform experiments**, but what would this horrible convenience cost them?

roundEndKnowledge.2.full: The townsfolk chose to remain ignorant of the technological advances of the age. Not only did they begrudge and mistrust the wealth of knowledge that the cousins had accrued, they hated them for it.
roundEndKnowledge.2.easy: The townspeople chose to stay ignorant about the new technology of their time. They did not only envy and distrust the great knowledge the cousins had collected; they hated them for it.
roundEndKnowledge.2.short: The townsfolk shunned modern technology, and hated the cousins for their knowledge.

roundEndKnowledge.3.full: The hostility had not abated. If anything, time had proven the townsfolk steadfast in their unsophisticated point of view. The perils of blind faith and excessive drink manifested in the gloom that surrounded the ashen streets.
roundEndKnowledge.3.easy: The anger had not gone away. If anything, time had shown that the townspeople held on firmly to their simple way of thinking. The dangers of blind faith and too much alcohol could be seen in the gloom around the gray streets.
roundEndKnowledge.3.short: The hostility endured; blind faith and drink hung like gloom over the ashen streets.

roundEndKnowledge.4.full: Each player gains **1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}** for **each** Knowledge cube in their Quarters.

It was as if some occult power had a hold over their senses. This nausea quickly turned to resolve and some even questioned why they had ever doubted the veracity of the Hunters' claims.

This sickness quickly turned into certainty, and some even asked themselves why they had ever doubted that the Hunters were telling the truth.
CannotParticipate.3.short: In the evenings before, some grew ill at the very thought of confronting the Hunters, as if an occult power held them, and began to wonder why they had ever doubted them.

CannotParticipate.4.full: But, how could their parents have envisioned a strong curse would have been placed upon them when they decided to accept the **cure** so many years ago?
CannotParticipate.4.easy: But how could their parents have known that a strong curse would be put on them when they decided to accept the **cure** so many years ago?

Pricolici.2.easy: Only when they were less than a meter away, in that thick, old undergrowth, did the dark shape show itself to {0} III. It stood up from where it was crouching on a fallen tree, half-man and half-beast, much taller than the hunting party.
Pricolici.2.short: Less than a meter away in the undergrowth, a dark form rose from a fallen tree to tower over {0} III's party: half-man, half-beast.

Pricolici.3.full: Its body was covered head to toe with matted fur, and the face exposed an elongated snout flanked by eyes that shone like feral gas lamps. A being from folklore made flesh - a Pricolici! And there it waited, and watched, hovering in a space between one breath and the next, poised to flee or charge at a moment’s notice.
Pricolici.3.easy: Its whole body was covered in dirty, tangled fur. Its face had a long snout, with eyes on each side that shone like wild gas lamps. A creature from old stories, now real: a Pricolici! And there it waited and watched, frozen between one breath and the next, ready to run away or attack at any moment.
Pricolici.3.short: Matted fur, an elongated snout, eyes like feral gas lamps: a Pricolici from folklore made flesh! It watched, poised to flee or charge.

Moon Presence.2.full: The impenetrable haze swirled at its center like a small vortex, alive and billowing, before revealing a massive beast bathed in smoky luminescence. More than twice the size of any hunter in the group, it stood on reptilian hindquarters, scales speckled with moss and fungus oozing with a putrid sheen.
Moon Presence.2.easy: The thick fog turned in the middle like a small whirlpool, alive and moving, and then a huge beast appeared, glowing in the smoke. It was more than twice as big as any hunter in the group. It stood on the back legs of a reptile, and its scales were covered with moss and with fungus that dripped a stinking slime.
Moon Presence.2.short: The haze swirled into a vortex, revealing a beast twice a hunter's height, standing on reptilian legs, its scales oozing moss and fungus.

Moon Presence.3.full: And where a face should have been, only a dark, empty abyss could be seen, surrounded by a nest of thick, oily tentacles — a dark headdress of serpents floating in space, unnatural and unseeing, yet devilish to behold. And thus the **Moonlight Presence** made itself known.
Moon Presence.3.easy: Where its face should have been, there was only a dark, empty hole, surrounded by a nest of thick, oily tentacles, like a dark crown of snakes floating in the air: unnatural and blind, but evil to look at. This is how the **Moonlight Presence** showed itself.
Moon Presence.3.short: Where a face should be, only a dark abyss ringed by oily tentacles writhing like serpents. Thus the **Moonlight Presence** made itself known.

Wight.2.full: The stifling mist dissolved before {0} III as the oily black eyes of a hideous visage glinted in the pale moonlight. Under the boughs of a dying black locust tree, a **shambling wight** appeared. The ground beneath his broken toes withered to ash with each of his belabored steps. Somehow, the hunting party would need to vanquish this foul terror before the night was over.
Wight.2.easy: The thick fog disappeared in front of {0} III, and the oily black eyes of a horrible face shone in the pale moonlight. Under the branches of a dying black locust tree, a **shambling wight** appeared. With each of its slow, heavy steps, the ground under its broken toes turned to ash. Somehow, the hunting party had to defeat this terrible creature before the night was over.
Wight.2.short: The mist parted before {0} III. Under a dying locust tree, oily black eyes glinted: a **shambling wight**, the ground turning to ash beneath its broken toes. The party must vanquish it before dawn.

Troll.2.full: As they approached a small stone bridgeway spanning a dried up creek bed, a foul odor hung heavy in the air, chokingly thick. It was not long before the source became apparent as an ancient Troll clambered out from under the bridge, taking up position in front of it as though to block the way.
Troll.2.easy: As they came near a small stone bridge over a dry stream, a disgusting smell hung heavy in the air, so thick that it made them choke. Soon they saw where it came from: an ancient Troll climbed out from under the bridge and stood in front of it, as if to block the way.
Troll.2.short: At a stone bridge over a dry creek, a choking stench announced an ancient Troll, which climbed out to block the way.

Troll.3.full: Its blue-gray hair reached its knees, rope-like and covered with mud and leaves. From the tangle of wild hair emerged two massive arms with two equally massive hammers clutched in each hand. Its pock-marked, asymmetrical face loomed with anger in their direction.
Troll.3.easy: Its blue-gray hair hung down to its knees, like ropes, full of mud and leaves. Out of the wild hair came two huge arms, each holding an equally huge hammer. Its ugly, scarred face looked at them with anger.
Troll.3.short: Its knee-length, mud-caked hair hid two massive arms, each wielding a hammer. Its pock-marked face glared at them.

Golem.2.full: A concussive pounding echoed down through the canyon. Upon a darkened ridge not a furlong away, stood a colossus of aggravated rock that could have been hewn from the mountain itself: a Stone Golem!
Golem.2.easy: A loud pounding echoed down through the canyon. On a dark ridge, less than two hundred meters away, stood a giant of angry rock that looked as if it had been cut out of the mountain itself: a Stone Golem!
Golem.2.short: Pounding echoed through the canyon. On a ridge nearby stood a colossus of rock: a Stone Golem!

Golem.3.full: Its massive fists smashed repeatedly into a crater of its own making, and so preoccupied was it in this endeavor, the danger in approaching was not in being seen but in avoiding the boulders it sent plummeting down in all directions.
Golem.3.easy: It hit a crater it had made itself again and again with its huge fists. It was so busy with this that the danger in coming closer was not being seen, but being hit by the big rocks it sent flying in all directions.
Golem.3.short: It pounded a crater with its fists, so absorbed that the danger lay not in being seen, but in the boulders it sent flying.

Manticore.2.full: The ever-thinning air became filled with dust and smoke, followed by a terrifying roar that sent tremors of fear through all who heard it. A massive beast with a lion’s frame and giant’s head loomed above the path ahead, stirring up a cloud of debris in its wake.
Manticore.2.easy: The air, which was getting thinner and thinner, filled with dust and smoke, and then came a terrible roar that made everyone who heard it shake with fear. A huge beast with the body of a lion and the head of a giant rose above the path in front of them, and a cloud of dirt flew up behind it.
Manticore.2.short: Dust and smoke, then a terrifying roar: a beast with a lion's body and a giant's head loomed over the path.

Manticore.3.full: The Manticore landed heavily on the narrow path, folded back its leathery wings, and stood perched upon the stone expectantly. Smiling hungrily through a distorted human face that revealed countless needle-sharp teeth, it whipped its barbed tail in malevolent anticipation.
Manticore.3.easy: The Manticore landed heavily on the narrow path, folded back its leathery wings and stood on the rock, waiting. It smiled hungrily with a twisted human face full of countless needle-sharp teeth, and it swung its spiked tail, looking forward to what would come.
Manticore.3.short: The Manticore landed, folding its leathery wings. Its distorted human face smiled hungrily with needle teeth, its barbed tail lashing.

Strigoi.2.full: As they approached the darkened alley, they heard first the hideous sound of an animal hungrily feeding on a fresh kill. Peering down the alley, the sound immediately ceased as torchlight revealed a pale-skinned creature hovering over the eviscerated body of an unfortunate townsfolk.
Strigoi.2.easy: As they came near the dark alley, they first heard the terrible sound of an animal eating a fresh kill hungrily. When they looked into the alley, the sound stopped at once, and the torchlight showed a pale-skinned creature bent over the torn-open body of an unlucky townsperson.
Strigoi.2.short: From a dark alley came the sound of feeding. Torchlight revealed a pale creature hunched over a disembowelled townsperson.

Strigoi.3.full: It spun to face them, baring long, white fangs and hissing like a cornered housecat. Its red, hateful eyes narrowed as it prepared to strike; its gangly torso was covered neck to waist in a glistening liquid. There was no doubt that this abomination was a **Strigoi**. It would appear the tales were true.
Strigoi.3.easy: It turned to face them, showed its long white fangs and hissed like a trapped house cat. Its red, hateful eyes became narrow as it got ready to attack; its long, thin body was covered from neck to waist in a shiny liquid. There was no doubt: this monster was a **Strigoi**. It seemed the stories were true.
Strigoi.3.short: It spun, baring long fangs and hissing, red eyes narrowed, its gangly torso glistening. This was a **Strigoi**. The tales were true.

Priest.2.full: The doors to the church swung inward with great force as though pulled at the end by an unseen hand. A figure in dark robes stood at the pulpit, his unnatural voice echoing a solemn incantation.
Priest.2.easy: The church doors swung open with great force, as if an invisible hand had pulled them. A figure in dark robes stood at the pulpit, and his unnatural voice echoed as he spoke a serious magic spell.
Priest.2.short: The church doors flew open as if pulled by an unseen hand. A robed figure at the pulpit chanted in an unnatural voice.

Priest.3.full: Positioned like sentinels, marble statues flanked the apse, their eyes leaking blood that pooled red and bright on the floor below. When {0} III looked again to the figure at the altar, the Priest had turned towards them, arms held high. His hood pulled back to reveal a disfigured face, hairless, lipless and smiling grotesquely, glossy with a sheen of fresh blood.
Priest.3.easy: Marble statues stood on both sides of the apse like guards, and blood ran from their eyes into bright red pools on the floor. When {0} III looked at the figure at the altar again, the Priest had turned towards them with his arms raised high. His hood fell back and showed a damaged face, without hair and without lips, smiling horribly and shining with fresh blood.
Priest.3.short: Statues wept blood beside the apse. The Priest turned to {0} III, arms raised, his hood falling back on a hairless, lipless face that grinned, glossy with fresh blood.

OptiontoKillYes.2.full: While I struggle to insinuate such an onerous deed, the cousins were correct in assuming the worst. Whether intentional or merely a byproduct of the stresses of advanced aging on the mind, there would soon be horrible and unknowable consequences for unnaturally extending one's existence.
OptiontoKillYes.2.easy: I find it hard to suggest such a terrible act, but the cousins were right to expect the worst. Whether on purpose, or just because old age puts so much stress on the mind, making your life unnaturally long would soon have terrible and unknown consequences.
OptiontoKillYes.2.short: Hard as it is to say, the cousins rightly feared the worst: unnaturally extended life would soon bring terrible consequences.

Not only did they describe a feeling of anxiety from their constant negativity and criticism, but there was a growing fear that they were actively sabotaging the experiments.
OptiontoKillStart.2.easy: During this time, the cousins' diaries became more and more suspicious about the work of their surprisingly strong parents. They wrote about feeling nervous because their parents were always negative and critical, and also about a growing fear that the parents were secretly ruining their experiments.
OptiontoKillStart.2.short: The cousins' journals grew paranoid about their hardy parents: not just constant criticism, but fear of active sabotage.

OptiontoKillStart.3.full: Coincidentally, several journal entries, dated over the course of the first months in the year of 1891, form a collective study on human anatomy. Contained within these pages are detailed sketches of exposed muscle fibers with cross-sections of the various strains upon veins and arteries. The age of the subject is especially advanced, providing exceptional clarity on how this has affected the structure and blood flow of these areas.
OptiontoKillStart.3.easy: By chance, several diary entries from the first months of the year 1891 form one study of the human body. These pages have detailed drawings of open muscle fibers, with cross-sections showing the different kinds of strain on veins and arteries. The subject is very old, which shows especially clearly how age has changed the structure and the blood flow in these parts of the body.
OptiontoKillStart.3.short: Coincidentally, journal entries from early 1891 form an anatomical study: detailed sketches of muscle and veins in a subject of very advanced age.

GloomyWolvesIntro.3.full: I will attempt to relay the events as they were explained to me, though I fully understand the solemn repercussions of the unfathomable knowledge contained within this text.
GloomyWolvesIntro.3.easy: I will try to tell the events as they were explained to me, even though I fully understand the serious consequences of the unbelievable knowledge in this text.
GloomyWolvesIntro.3.short: I will relay events as they were told to me, knowing the grave weight of what this text contains.

GloomyWolvesIntro.4.full: Amongst the forests of the Romanian countryside, nestled in shadowed valleys of the Carpathian mountains, there are places so far removed from the rest of the world as to appear almost invisible in their machinations. In shadows tucked away amongst the deepest tangled forests, from the darkest crevices burrowed deep into the earth, these are the places where our most pervasive legends and folklore emerge. And in their isolation, it grows.
GloomyWolvesIntro.4.easy: In the forests of the Romanian countryside, hidden in the dark valleys of the Carpathian mountains, there are places so far from the rest of the world that what happens there is almost invisible. In the shadows of the deepest, thickest forests, in the darkest cracks deep in the earth: these are the places where our strongest legends and folk tales come from. And because they are so isolated, they grow.
GloomyWolvesIntro.4.short: In the shadowed valleys of the Carpathians lie places so remote they are almost invisible. From their deepest forests and darkest crevices our legends emerge, and in isolation, they grow.

GloomyWolvesIntro.5.full: The next generation's return was marked by a most startling and terrifying discovery. For it appeared that while the disease had left the town, another more insidious plague had befallen the land. The Order of St. Hubertus, emboldened by the success of their clandestine labors, took the opportunity afforded them and manifested in their true and cursed forms. And like the emblematic wolfhead adorning their insignia, they arose with silvered pelts, baring distended fangs and open animalistic maws that dripped with saliva. The least horrifying held this form at least, as the other beasts hosted swelling deformities and twisted extremities too repulsive to describe. The ancient evils they had unearthed from beneath the town gave them the ability to transform without the full moon's glow, and in the light of day, these monstrous beings set upon the townsfolk to enforce their rule either by coercion or by visceral and bloody execution.
GloomyWolvesIntro.5.easy: When the next generation came back, they made a very surprising and frightening discovery. The disease had left the town, but another, more evil plague had come over the land. The Order of St. Hubertus, made bold by the success of their secret work, used their chance and showed themselves in their true, cursed forms. Like the wolf's head on their sign, they rose up with silver fur, long fangs and open animal mouths dripping with spit. And these were the least horrible ones: the other beasts had growing deformities and twisted limbs too disgusting to describe. The ancient evil they had dug up from under the town let them change their shape without the light of the full moon. In broad daylight, these monsters attacked the townspeople to force them to obey, either with threats or with bloody executions.
GloomyWolvesIntro.5.short: The next generation returned to a terrifying discovery: the disease was gone, but a worse plague had come. The Order of St. Hubertus revealed its cursed forms: silver-pelted wolves with dripping fangs, and worse deformities besides. Ancient evils let them transform by day, and they ruled the town by coercion or bloody execution.

GloomyWolvesIntro.7.full: But as the Order expanded its numbers and influence, the beasts did not recognize their new forms as folly. They called themselves "Strigoi" (embracing the vampiric moniker given them by local folklore) and commanded quick control over the local government. To them, they were the powerful new evolution of society. They perceived humanity as the real monster!
GloomyWolvesIntro.7.easy: But as the Order grew in numbers and power, the beasts did not see their new forms as a mistake. They called themselves "Strigoi" (accepting the vampire name that local folk tales gave them) and quickly took control of the local government. In their eyes, they were the powerful next step of society. To them, humanity was the real monster!
GloomyWolvesIntro.7.short: As the Order grew, the beasts embraced their forms, calling themselves "Strigoi" after the local vampire legend, and seized the government. Humanity, to them, was the real monster!

GloomyWolvesIntro.8.full: However, they were not unkeen to the important work of the family. In fact, they took a great interest in their experimentations, even to the point of offering their assistance. And as the new generation was thrust into this distorted new reality, they were forced to consider a most dreadful prospect: to aid these creatures in their scheme and spread their message of dreadful bloodlust or incur their loathsome wrath.
GloomyWolvesIntro.8.easy: But they did know about the family's important work. In fact, they were very interested in their experiments, and even offered their help. And as the new generation was pushed into this twisted new world, they had to think about a terrible choice: help these creatures with their plan and spread their message of terrible bloodlust, or face their horrible anger.
GloomyWolvesIntro.8.short: But they took a keen interest in the family's experiments, even offering help. The new generation faced a dreadful choice: aid the creatures and spread their bloodlust, or incur their wrath.

Preposterous.2.full: Despite their proclivities towards what other weaker willed individuals might call "a mad, unending exploration of a vile and unethical pseudoscience by the frightfully inexperienced," the youthful generation had one unyielding virtue: they were very rich. And the rich definitely do not pay taxes.
Preposterous.2.easy: Other, weaker people might call their work "a mad, endless exploration of a disgusting and immoral false science by frighteningly inexperienced people". But the young generation had one strong advantage: they were very rich. And rich people definitely do not pay taxes.
Preposterous.2.short: Whatever weaker minds called their "mad, unending exploration of a vile pseudoscience", the young generation had one virtue: they were very rich. And the rich do not pay taxes.

Preposterous.3.full: While a sort of hysteria may have gripped their frail psyche, the very idea that {0} noted aristocrats would pay a penalty for the privilege of living amongst these rabble without a significant guarantee of return on investment was more absurd than the rumors of a portal opened to the netherworld.
Preposterous.3.easy: Maybe some kind of panic had taken hold of their weak minds, but the idea that {0} famous aristocrats would pay a fee for the honor of living among these common people, without a good guarantee that they would get something back, was more ridiculous than the rumors about a door to the underworld.
Preposterous.3.short: That {0} noted aristocrats should pay to live among this rabble, with no guaranteed return, was more absurd than rumors of a portal to the netherworld.

TheVialUse.2.full: Clearly, there were no others strong enough to thwart the evil that had taken over the valley and spread across the forests of Hungary. {0} III returned to their home with determination in their chest and retrieved the crystal **vial** now displayed above their hearth.
TheVialUse.2.easy: Clearly, nobody else was strong enough to stop the evil that had taken over the valley and spread across the forests of Hungary. {0} III went home, determined, and took the crystal **vial** that now stood above their fireplace.
TheVialUse.2.short: No one else could stop the evil spreading across Hungary's forests. Resolute, {0} III took the crystal **vial** from above their hearth.

TheVialUse.3.full: With this vial of the most blessed of holy waters, they knew they could take matters into their own hands and righteously reclaim the land once lost.
TheVialUse.3.easy: With this small bottle of the holiest water, they knew they could act themselves and rightfully win back the land that had been lost.
TheVialUse.3.short: With this holy water, they could reclaim the lost land themselves.

TheVialUse.4.full: Alternatively and suspiciously well-timed, a traveling caravan had offered a significant sum for it recently. But, of course, ridding the land of all evil was the most pressing of matters.
TheVialUse.4.easy: On the other hand, and at a suspiciously good moment, a traveling caravan had recently offered a lot of money for it. But of course, freeing the land from all evil was the most important thing.
TheVialUse.4.short: Then again, a traveling caravan had recently, and suspiciously, offered a large sum for it. But ridding the land of evil came first, of course.

VialCharity.6.full: While inspecting a wooden shelf in the pantry, the unexpected clatter of crystal on stone shook the young {0} III. Luckily, it appeared the vial of liquid remained undamaged, although the paper tag attached to the cork stopper at its top was of considerable age.
VialCharity.6.easy: While the young {0} III was looking at a wooden shelf in the pantry, the unexpected sound of crystal falling on stone gave them a shock. Luckily, the small bottle of liquid seemed to be undamaged, but the paper label on its cork was very old.
VialCharity.6.short: A clatter of crystal on stone startled {0} III in the pantry. The vial was unharmed, though its tag was very old.

VialCharity.7.full: The note stated, "A gift of Holy Water from a thankful church of God," and was aptly addressed to {0} the 1st. Interestingly, it had remained stored away since the charitable events of the long past.
VialCharity.7.easy: The note said: "A gift of Holy Water from a thankful church of God," and it was addressed, fittingly, to {0} the 1st. Interestingly, it had been stored away ever since the charity work long ago.
VialCharity.7.short: It read, "A gift of Holy Water from a thankful church of God," addressed to {0} the 1st, stored away since that long-ago charity.

VialSold.2.full: To look back on this moment with pure hindsight and recognize that a being had the potential to halt this insidious infestation and chose instead to turn the situation into a financial windfall is harrowing. {0} III's infamous decision would result in a blight upon the land that was nigh unstoppable.
VialSold.2.easy: It is terrible to look back on this moment and see that someone had the power to stop this evil plague, but chose to make money out of it instead. {0} III's famous decision would bring a curse over the land that almost nothing could stop.
VialSold.2.short: It is harrowing that one who could halt the infestation chose profit instead. {0} III's infamous decision brought a near-unstoppable blight upon the land.

VialChanged.2.full: The liquid was introduced at the source of the stream that winded through the hoary gloom enveloping the town of {0}. Like a glittering oil, it spread downstream, turning the murky waters clear once again with a supernatural effervescence.
VialChanged.2.easy: They poured the liquid into the source of the stream that ran through the gray gloom around the town of {0}. Like shiny oil, it spread down the stream and made the dark water clear again with a magical sparkle.
VialChanged.2.short: Poured into the stream's source above {0}, the liquid spread like glittering oil, turning the murky waters clear.

VialChanged.3.full: After less than a day's passing, the azalea blossoms that once dotted the landscape were in full bloom and the radiant sunlight bathed the valley in a honey glow. The creatures that remained found themselves reformed, though still horrific to behold, and went about clothed in dapper suits and summer dresses with hats that could easily be tipped as a friendly greeting.
VialChanged.3.easy: In less than a day, the azalea flowers that once grew all over the land were in full bloom, and bright sunlight covered the valley in a golden glow. The creatures that were left were changed for the better, but still horrible to look at. They walked around in smart suits and summer dresses, with hats that they could lift as a friendly greeting.
VialChanged.3.short: Within a day, the azaleas bloomed and sunlight bathed the valley. The remaining creatures, reformed if still horrific, strolled about in suits and summer dresses, tipping their hats.

VialChanged.4.full: Those of the Order that refused to submit to the cleansing beauty fled into the hills never to be seen again. The cousins were free once again to be the most unconventional presences within the town, and returned to their labors with no further interruptions.
VialChanged.4.easy: The members of the Order who refused to accept the cleansing beauty ran away into the hills and were never seen again. The cousins were once again free to be the strangest people in town, and they went back to their work without any more disturbances.
VialChanged.4.short: Those of the Order who refused fled into the hills, never to be seen again. The cousins were once more the town's oddest residents, and returned to work undisturbed.

Gen1Creepy-ConcealExpose.8.full: "We have decided to forgive your family's debt to us due to your recent pledge of loyalty. I was sent to offer this word of salutation and reminder that we are pleased. Consider this canceled debt as our gift to you." The man, with a ceremonial air, then lifted a piece of parchment before him and, with a quick slice, let the cleaved paper fall to the stone steps.
Gen1Creepy-ConcealExpose.8.easy: "Because you recently promised us your loyalty, we have decided to forgive your family's debt to us. I was sent to greet you and to remind you that we are happy with you. This canceled debt is our gift to you." Then, as if in a ceremony, the man held up a piece of paper and, with one quick cut, let the two halves fall to the stone steps.
Gen1Creepy-ConcealExpose.8.short: "For your pledge of loyalty, we forgive your family's debt. Consider it our gift." Ceremonially, the man sliced a parchment in two and let it fall to the steps.

ProsperityWolvesIntro.4.full: Could a period of prosperity emerge like a blooming lily in the shadow of a headstone? Could it thrive in soil so enriched by disease and death? With the evil machinations exposed and banished from the town, the Order of St. Hubertus was quick to answer these questions with reforms that cleared the smog and grayness from the streets. They tilled the fields till the beet flowers sprung from the earth, encouraged trade with nearby towns, and embraced modern conveniences, even so far as to negotiate an extension of the national electrical power grid. The youths, upon returning from university to claim their inheritance, could scarcely recognize the village from their childhood.
ProsperityWolvesIntro.4.easy: Could a time of wealth grow like a lily flowering in the shadow of a gravestone? Could it grow in soil so full of disease and death? After the evil plans were exposed and sent away from the town, the Order of St. Hubertus quickly answered these questions with reforms that cleared the smoke and grayness from the streets. They worked the fields until the beet flowers grew, encouraged trade with nearby towns and welcomed modern comforts. They even arranged a connection to the national electricity network. When the young people came back from university to receive their inheritance, they could hardly recognize the village of their childhood.
ProsperityWolvesIntro.4.short: Could prosperity bloom like a lily beside a headstone? With the evil banished, the Order of St. Hubertus answered with reforms: clean streets, flowering fields, trade, even electricity. Returning from university, the heirs barely recognized their childhood village.

ProsperityWolvesIntro.5.full: But, it soon became clear why they were so determined to be accepted and improve their reputation. For one evening, when the blood moon crossed the evening sky, they transformed, revealing the monstrous beings they had kept secret for so many years as the unafflicted in the town looked on in horror.
ProsperityWolvesIntro.5.easy: But it soon became clear why they wanted so badly to be accepted and to improve their reputation. One evening, when the blood moon crossed the sky, they changed, and showed the monsters they had kept secret for so many years, while the healthy people of the town watched in horror.
ProsperityWolvesIntro.5.short: But one evening, under a blood moon, it became clear why: they transformed into the monsters they had long hidden, before the horrified town.

ProsperityWolvesIntro.7.full: But the beasts did not recognize their new forms as folly. Though their bodies shifted into monstrosities more animal than man - more wolven, with sharp features, claws, and steel-eyed gazes - they pleaded with the public for compassion. Should we not celebrate that which makes us different? Is it not these differences that allow us to grow stronger together?
ProsperityWolvesIntro.7.easy: But the beasts did not see their new forms as a mistake. Their bodies changed into monsters, more animal than human, more like wolves, with sharp features, claws and hard eyes, but they asked the people for understanding. Should we not celebrate what makes us different? Do these differences not help us to grow stronger together?
ProsperityWolvesIntro.7.short: The beasts saw no folly in their wolven forms of claw and steel-eyed gaze. They pleaded for compassion: should we not celebrate our differences, which make us stronger together?
